description.en: Engkanto (from Spanish encanto, lit. 'enchantment') are mythical environmental spirits that are said to have the ability to appear in human form. They are often associated with the spirits of ancestors and spirits of the dead called anito in the Philippines. They are also characterized as spirit sorts like sirens, dark beings, elves, and more. Belief in their existence has likely existed for centuries, and continues to this day. It is a bracket term for enchanted human-like beings of the land which includes a variety of mythical races. The term itself was adopted from the Spanish, who were dumbfounded by the wide array of mythical races in the Philippines and just referred to many of the races as "enchanted". Though at the same time the term does not differ at all from the archaic Spanish sense of the word as referring to a supernatural apparition, sometimes tied to a place. Francisco Demetrio made a study of 87 folk stories from Visayas and Mindanao relating to engkanto. He contended that the engkanto were based on early European friars.

description.en: In Finnish folklore, all places and things, and also human beings, have a haltija (a genie, guardian spirit) of their own. One such haltija is called etiäinen—an image, doppelgänger, or just an impression that goes ahead of a person, doing things the person in question later does. For example, people waiting for someone at home might hear the door close, as if the one they are waiting for arrived, or even see their shadow or a silhouette, only to realize that they have not arrived yet after all. When the person finally comes home, they would repeat the actions of their etiäinen that the people waiting witnessed earlier. Etiäinen can also refer to some kind of a feeling that something is going to happen. Sometimes it could, for example, warn of a bad year coming. In modern Finnish, the term has detached from its shamanistic origins and refers to premonition. Unlike clairvoyance, divination, and similar practices, etiäiset (plural) are spontaneous and cannot be induced. Quite the opposite, they may be unwanted and cause anxiety, like ghosts. Etiäiset may concern everyday events and are not necessarily too dramatic, although ones related to deaths are not uncommon either. As these phenomena are still reported today, they can be considered a living tradition, as a way to explain the psychological experience of premonition.

claims.statement: In Finnish folklore all places, things and people have a haltija (guardian spirit); one is the etiäinen, an image, doppelgänger or impression that goes ahead of a person doing what they later do.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Finlandia, semua tempat, benda, dan manusia punya haltija (roh penjaga); salah satunya etiäinen, bayangan, kembaran, atau kesan yang mendahului seseorang dan melakukan hal yang kelak ia lakukan.
claims.quote: In Finnish folklore, all places and things, and also human beings, have a haltija (a genie, guardian spirit) of their own.  One such haltija is called etiäinen—an image, doppelgänger, or just an impression that goes ahead of a person, doing things the person in question later does.

claims.statement: Etiäinen can also mean a feeling that something is going to happen, for example a warning of a bad year coming.
claims.statement_id: Etiäinen juga bisa berarti perasaan bahwa sesuatu akan terjadi, misalnya peringatan akan datangnya tahun yang buruk.
claims.quote: Etiäinen can also refer to some kind of a feeling that something is going to happen. Sometimes it could, for example, warn of a bad year coming.

claims.statement: In modern Finnish the term has left its shamanistic origins and means premonition; etiäiset (plural) are spontaneous, cannot be induced, and may be unwanted and cause anxiety, like ghosts.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Finlandia modern istilah ini lepas dari asal syamanistiknya dan berarti firasat; etiäiset (jamak) bersifat spontan, tidak bisa dipanggil, dan dapat tidak diinginkan serta menimbulkan kecemasan seperti hantu.
claims.quote: In modern Finnish, the term has detached from its shamanistic origins and refers to premonition. Unlike clairvoyance, divination, and similar practices, etiäiset (plural) are spontaneous and cannot be induced. Quite the opposite, they may be unwanted and cause anxiety, like ghosts.

claims.statement: People may hear a family member walk into the yard and open the door, even see their figure or shadow, then realise they have not come; soon the person arrives and repeats what their etiäinen did.
claims.statement_id: Orang bisa mendengar anggota keluarganya masuk halaman dan membuka pintu, bahkan melihat sosok atau bayangannya, lalu sadar ia belum datang; tak lama ia benar-benar datang dan mengulangi apa yang dilakukan etiäinen-nya.
claims.quote: Ihmiset saattavat kuulla esimerkiksi perheenjäsenensä kävelevän pihaan, avaavan oven, jopa nähdä tämän hahmon tai varjon, kunnes huomaavat, ettei tämä todellisuudessa vielä tullutkaan. Pian perheenjäsen kuitenkin tulee ja toistaa saman kuin etiäisensä.

claims.statement: The etiäinen is received at three days old and follows its person's character traits.
claims.statement_id: Etiäinen diperoleh pada usia tiga hari dan mengikuti watak pemiliknya.
claims.quote: Etiäinen saadaan kolmen päivän vanhana, ja se noudattaa ihmisensä luonteenpiirteitä.

claims.statement: Vardøger is the Norwegian etiäinen.
claims.statement_id: Vardøger adalah etiäinen versi Norwegia.
claims.quote: Vardøger, norjalainen etiäinen

description.en: In folklore and literature, the Fairy Queen or Queen of the Fairies is a female ruler of the fairies, sometimes but not always paired with a king. Depending on the work, she may be named or unnamed; Titania and Mab are two frequently used names. Numerous characters, goddesses or folkloric spirits worldwide have been labeled as Fairy Queens.

claims.statement: The Fairy Queen (Queen of the Fairies) is a female ruler of fairies, sometimes with a king; named Titania or Mab.
claims.statement_id: Fairy Queen (Queen of the Fairies) penguasa perempuan peri, kadang berpasangan raja; nama Titania dan Mab; di Britania dan Irlandia.
claims.quote: In folklore and literature, the Fairy Queen or Queen of the Fairies is a female ruler of the fairies, sometimes but not always paired with a king. Depending on the work, she may be named or unnamed; Titania and Mab are two frequently used names.

claims.statement: The Tuatha Dé Danann and Daoine Sidhe of Irish myth had many kings and queens; Oonagh (Una, Nuala) was wife of Finvarra, fairy king of western Ireland.
claims.statement_id: Tuatha Dé Danann dan Daoine Sidhe mitologi Irlandia (Irish) punya banyak raja-ratu; Oonagh (Una, Nuala) istri Finvarra, raja peri Irlandia (Ireland) barat.
claims.quote: The Tuatha Dé Danann and the Daoine Sidhe of Irish mythology had numerous local kings and queens. Oonagh, Una or Nuala was the wife of Finvarra or Fionnbharr, the fairy king of western Ireland

claims.statement: Other Irish fairy queens: Clíodhna of Munster, Aibhell, Ainé.

claims.quote: Other Irish fairy queens included Clíodhna of Munster, Aibhell and Ainé.

claims.statement: Arthurian Morgan le Fey ruled Avalon and was sometimes a fairy queen; in the Vita Merlini, Morgen heads nine queens.
claims.statement_id: Morgan le Fey (Arthurian) memerintah Avalon, kadang ratu peri; dalam Vita Merlini, Morgen kepala sembilan ratu.
claims.quote: The Arthurian character of Morgan le Fey (or Morgan of the Fairies) ruled the supernatural island of Avalon and was sometimes depicted as a fairy queen. In the Vita Merlini , she is Morgen, the chief of nine magical sister queens.

claims.statement: A kind fairy queen in Alison Gross, a deadly one in Tam Lin who pays a tithe to Hell every seven years; Child Ballads.
claims.statement_id: Ratu peri baik dalam Alison Gross, kejam dalam Tam Lin yang membayar upeti ke Neraka (Hell) tiap tujuh tahun; Child Ballads.
claims.quote: A kind and helpful fairy queen features in Alison Gross (Child 35), and a terrible and deadly fairy queen is the antagonist of Tam Lin (Child 39). Tam Lin's Fairy Queen pays a tithe to Hell every seven years

claims.statement: In Thomas the Rhymer a fairy queen takes Thomas as lover and gives him prophetic powers.

claims.quote: An unnamed fairy queen appears in Thomas the Rhymer (Child 37), where she takes the titular character as her lover and leaves him with prophetic abilities.

claims.statement: Fairy queens (reinas de las hadas) appear in the Child Ballads, 305 folk ballads of England (Inglaterra) and Scotland (Escocia) collected by Francis James Child.
claims.statement_id: Reina de las hadas muncul dalam Child Ballads, 305 balada rakyat Inggris (Inglaterra) dan Skotlandia (Escocia) himpunan Francis James Child.
claims.quote: Las reinas de las hadas aparecen en algunas de las Baladas Infantiles, un conjunto de 305 baladas populares de Inglaterra y Escocia recopiladas por Francis James Child.

description.en: A far darrig or fear dearg is a faerie type in Irish mythology. The name far darrig is an Anglophone pronunciation of the Irish words fear dearg, meaning Red Man, as the far darrig is said to wear a red coat and cap. They are sometimes known as Rat Boys as they are said to be rather fat, have dark, hairy skin, long snouts and skinny tails. The far derrig is generally described as short, while sometimes described as tall. It's said the far derrig has the ability to change sizes. An 1832 description from T. Crofton Croaker in Munster says the far derrig are around 2.5 feet tall with a wrinkled face, long grey hair, and a sugarloaf hat. According to Fairy and Folk Tales of the Irish Peasantry, the far darrig is classified as a solitary fairy along with the leprechaun and the clurichaun, all of whom are "most sluttish, slouching, jeering, mischievous phantoms". The far darrig in particular is described as one who "busies himself with practical joking, especially with gruesome joking". One example of this is replacing babies with changelings. They are also said to have some connection to nightmares. Refusing any request from a far derrig was unlucky, as they were very imaginative in thinking of punishments. When not playing jokes, the far darrig spend much of their time smoking by campfires and thinking. They will eat a meal if offered, and the presence of one in a house is said to bring good luck.

claims.statement: The far darrig (fear dearg) is an Irish fairy, Red Man, in a red coat and cap; also called Rat Boys.
claims.statement_id: Far darrig (fear dearg) peri mitologi Irlandia (Irish), Lelaki Merah (Red Man), bermantel dan bertopi merah; juga Rat Boys; di Irlandia. Pelafalan Anglophone.

They are sometimes known as Rat Boys as they are said to be rather fat, have dark, hairy skin, long snouts and skinny tails.

claims.statement: Short or tall, can change size; T. Crofton Croker, Munster, 1832: about 2.5 feet, wrinkled face.

Crofton Croaker in Munster says the far derrig are around 2.5 feet tall with a wrinkled face, long grey hair, and a sugarloaf hat.

claims.statement: Fairy and Folk Tales of the Irish Peasantry: a solitary fairy with the leprechaun and clurichaun.
claims.statement_id: Fairy and Folk Tales of the Irish Peasantry: peri penyendiri bersama leprechaun (Leprechaun) dan clurichaun (Clurichaun).
claims.quote: According to Fairy and Folk Tales of the Irish Peasantry, the far darrig is classified as a solitary fairy along with the leprechaun and the clurichaun, all of whom are "most sluttish, slouching, jeering, mischievous phantoms".

claims.statement_id: Menolak permintaannya membawa sial.
claims.quote: Refusing any request from a far derrig was unlucky, as they were very imaginative in thinking of punishments.

claims.statement: Yeats: the Far Darrig (fear dearg), Red Man, in red cap and coat, busies himself with gruesome practical joking.
claims.statement_id: Yeats: Far Darrig (fear dearg), Red Man, bertopi dan bermantel merah, sibuk dengan lelucon keji; W. B. Yeats.
claims.quote: The Far Darrig (fear dearg), which means the Red Man, for he wears a red cap and coat, busies himself with practical joking, especially with gruesome joking.

claims.statement: He forces householders to take him in and give him the best place by the fire (coin du feu).
claims.statement_id: Ia memaksa penghuni rumah menerimanya dan memberinya tempat terbaik dekat perapian (coin du feu).
claims.quote: On dit de lui qu'il a tendance à forcer les habitants d'une maison à l'accueillir chez eux, et à lui réserver la meilleure place, au coin du feu.

claims.statement: For example, replacing babies with changelings.
claims.statement_id: Contohnya menukar bayi dengan changeling (Changeling).
claims.quote: One example of this is replacing babies with changelings.

description.en: Feilian (traditional Chinese: 飛廉; simplified Chinese: 飞廉; pinyin: fēilián) or (蜚廉) is a Chinese wind spirit from a southern tradition, later identified with and subsumed under the primary wind deity Fengbo. Feilian has also been identified with a late Shang dynasty minister as well as with the mythical phoenix bird, and retained a separate identity as a mythical creature after losing its status as master of the wind.

claims.statement: Feilian is a Chinese wind spirit from a southern tradition later linked to Fengbo.
claims.statement_id: Feilian adalah roh angin Tiongkok dari tradisi selatan yang kemudian dihubungkan dengan Fengbo.
claims.quote: Feilian (traditional Chinese: 飛廉; simplified Chinese: 飞廉; pinyin: fēilián) or (蜚廉) is a Chinese wind spirit from a southern tradition, later identified with and subsumed under the primary wind deity Fengbo.

claims.statement: The Li sao poem mentions Feilian assisting the poet's mystical journey.
claims.statement_id: Puisi Li sao menyebut Feilian sebagai penolong perjalanan mistis penyair.
claims.quote: Feilian is first attested in the influential poem Li sao by Qu Yuan, wherein Feilian assists the poet in part of his mystical journey. This work comes from Chu, a Zhou dynasty state which was on the periphery of the Zhou cultural sphere, and is typically dated to the 300s or 200s bce.

claims.statement: In his Fengbo identity, he carries wind in a bag.
claims.statement_id: Dalam identitas Fengbo, ia membawa angin dalam kantong.
claims.quote: In Feilian's identity as Fengbo, he carries wind with him in a bag and stirs up trouble. Feilian is kept in check by Houyi, the heavenly archer and Shang legendary culture hero. Feilian has become attached to the later mythology of the Yellow Emperor, against whom he contended under the leadership of Chiyou.

claims.statement: Houyi is portrayed as keeping Feilian in check.
claims.statement_id: Houyi digambarkan membatasi tindakan Feilian.
claims.quote: In Feilian's identity as Fengbo, he carries wind with him in a bag and stirs up trouble. Feilian is kept in check by Houyi, the heavenly archer and Shang legendary culture hero. Feilian has become attached to the later mythology of the Yellow Emperor, against whom he contended under the leadership of Chiyou.

claims.statement: Feilian was once believed able to grant immortality.
claims.statement_id: Feilian pernah dipercaya dapat memberikan keabadian.
claims.quote: Before consolidation into the Fengbo entity, Feilian was also thought to be able to grant immortality.

claims.statement: Emperor Wu of Han commissioned worship buildings in pursuit of that immortality.
claims.statement_id: Kaisar Wu dari Han mendirikan bangunan pemujaan untuk mengejar keabadian itu.
claims.quote: Emperor Wu of Han ... believed this sufficiently to order the construction of several buildings dedicated to Feilian worship in pursuit of this gift of eternal life.

description.id: Fenghuang (bahasa Mandarin: 鳳凰; pinyin: fènghuáng; bahasa Jepang: hōō; bahasa Korea: 봉황 bonghwang; bahasa Vietnam: Phượng Hoàng) adalah sebuah spesies burung dalam mitologi Tiongkok. Yang jantan disebut feng dan betina disebut huang. Dalam masa sekarang ini perbedaan kelamin tersebut jarang lagi dipakai. Fenghuang kerap ditemukan berpasangan dengan naga yang memiliki konotasi jantan. Di dunia barat, fenghuang sering dihubungkan dengan feniks. Di kalangan Tionghoa-Indonesia, Fenghuang sendiri biasanya dikenal dengan nama dalam dialek Hokkian-nya, hong. Biasanya dilafalkan berpasangan dengan naga sehingga dilafalkan menjadi leng-hong. Pada masa Tiongkok kuno, fenghuang sering ditemukan pada dekorasi pernikahan atau keluarga ningrat bersamaan dengan naga. Ini disebabkan tradisi Tiongkok yang menganggap naga dan feniks sebagai simbol hubungan yang mesra antara suami dan istri, sebuah bentuk metafora antara yin dan yang. Fenghuang juga adalah nama kabupaten di provinsi Hunan.
description.en: Fenghuang ( fung-HWAHNG) are mythological birds featuring in traditions throughout the Sinosphere. Fenghuang are understood to reign over all other birds: males and females were originally termed feng and huang respectively, but a gender distinction is typically no longer made, and fenghuang are generally considered a feminine entity to be paired with the traditionally masculine Chinese dragon. In the West, they are commonly called Chinese phoenixes, although mythological similarities with the Western/Persian phoenix are superficial.

claims.statement: Fenghuang are mythic birds found across traditions influenced by Chinese culture.
claims.statement_id: Fenghuang adalah burung mitologis yang dikenal dalam tradisi kawasan budaya Tiongkok.
claims.quote: Fenghuang (/fʌŋˈwɑːŋ/ fung-HWAHNG) are mythological birds featuring in traditions throughout the Sinosphere.

claims.statement: Fenghuang hold supremacy among birds and are often paired with dragons.
claims.statement_id: Fenghuang dianggap berkuasa atas burung lainnya dan sering dipasangkan dengan naga.
claims.quote: Fenghuang (/fʌŋˈwɑːŋ/ fung-HWAHNG) are mythological birds featuring in traditions throughout the Sinosphere.

claims.statement: Calling it a Chinese phoenix does not imply the same mythology as the Western phoenix.
claims.statement_id: Sebutan phoenix Tiongkok tidak berarti kisahnya sama dengan phoenix Barat.
claims.quote: In the West, they are commonly called Chinese phoenixes, although mythological similarities with the Western/Persian phoenix are superficial.

claims.statement: The Erya describes a composite anatomy including a rooster's beak and a snake's neck.
claims.statement_id: Erya menggambarkannya sebagai gabungan ciri berbagai hewan, termasuk paruh ayam dan leher ular.
claims.quote: A common depiction of fenghuang was of it attacking snakes with its talons and its wings spread. According to the Erya's chapter 17 Shiniao, fenghuang is made up of the beak of a rooster, the face of a swallow, the forehead of a fowl, the neck of a snake, the breast of a goose, the back of a tortoise, the hindquarters of a stag and the tail of a fish.

claims.statement: Its head, eyes, and back are associated with the sky, sun, and moon.
claims.statement_id: Kepala, mata, dan punggungnya dihubungkan dengan langit, matahari, dan bulan.
claims.quote: The fenghuang's body symbolizes the celestial bodies: the head is the sky, the eyes are the sun, the back is the moon, the wings are the wind, the feet are the earth, and the tail is the planets. The fenghuang is said to have originated in the sun. Its body contains the five fundamental colors: black, white, red, yellow, and green or blue.

claims.statement: One tradition locates its dwelling on Mount Danzuan in the southern mountains.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah tradisi menempatkan kediamannya di Gunung Danzuan di pegunungan selatan.
claims.quote: Chinese tradition cites it as living atop Mount Danzuan in the southern mountains.

description.en: The Feuermann (fire man; German: [ˈfɔɪ̯ɐˌman]; pl. Feuermänner), also Brennender, Brünnling, Brünnlinger, Brünnlig (all: burning one), brünnigs Mannli (burning manikin), Züsler (sg., pl.; flickering one or arsonist), and Glühender (glowing one), is a fiery ghost from German folklore, which is different from the will-o'-the-wisp (German Irrlicht) owing to its size: Feuermänner are rather big, while Irrlichter are rather small. An often recurring term for Feuermänner is glühende Männer (pl.; glowing men; die glühenden Männer; in dialect gloinige Männer, glöhnege Männer, glöänige Männer or jlönige Männer).

claims.statement: The Feuermann ('fire man'; also Brennender, Brünnling, Züsler, Glühender, glühende Männer) is a fiery ghost of German folklore, unlike the will-o'-the-wisp (Irrlicht) in size: Feuermänner are big, Irrlichter small.
claims.statement_id: Feuermann ("manusia api"; juga Brennender, Brünnling, Züsler, Glühender, glühende Männer) adalah hantu berapi dari cerita rakyat Jerman (German) yang berbeda dari will-o'-the-wisp (Irrlicht) karena ukurannya: Feuermänner agak besar, Irrlichter agak kecil.
claims.quote: is a fiery ghost from German folklore, which is different from the will-o'-the-wisp (German Irrlicht) owing to its size: Feuermänner are rather big, while Irrlichter are rather small.

claims.statement: Some are humanlike, such as a skeleton blazing inside or a leaden manikin with fire under its mantle; others a black man in a pillar of fire; it can change its height at will from gigantic to tiny.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian digambarkan mirip manusia, seperti kerangka yang menyala dari dalam atau lelaki kecil bermantel timah dengan api di bawahnya; ada pula lelaki hitam di dalam tiang api; ia dapat mengubah tingginya sesuka hati dari raksasa hingga kecil.
claims.quote: Some are described as rather humanoid, such as a human skeleton whose insides are blazing with fire, or as a leaden manikin wearing a leaden mantle blazing with fire underneath. Another description is of a black man inside a tall, wide pillar of fire, or a Feuermann who is half black, half fiery. It is able to change its height at will, varying from gigantic to diminutive.

claims.statement: The Feuermann may also appear nearly shapeless, as a (sometimes giant) sheaf of straw, a big floating light, a fireball, a pyramid, a snake or a fiery wheel; it is very fast and can rise to hover above the treetops.
claims.statement_id: Feuermann juga bisa tampil hampir tanpa bentuk, seperti berkas jerami (kadang raksasa), cahaya besar melayang, bola api, piramida, ular, atau roda api; ia sangat cepat dan dapat naik ke udara melayang di atas pucuk pohon.
claims.quote: Alternatively, the Feuermann also appears more or less shapeless like a (sometimes gigantic) sheaf or bundle of straw, a big floating light, a fiery ball, a pyramid, a snake, or a fiery wheel. The Feuermann is very quick and able to rise in the air so that it hovers above the treetops.

claims.statement: The Feuermann is seen as a sinner haunting the earth to atone for its life's sins; often a Grenzfrevler who moved a boundary stone with criminal intent and is damned to haunt that boundary.
claims.statement_id: Feuermann dianggap pendosa yang bergentayangan di bumi untuk menebus dosa semasa hidup; sering ia seorang Grenzfrevler yang memindahkan batu batas dengan niat jahat sehingga jiwanya dikutuk menghantui batas itu.
claims.quote: It is seen as a sinner remaining hauntingly on earth to repent for its sins during lifetime. Frequently, the Feuermann is a so-called Grenzfrevler (sg., pl.) or boundary sinner who has moved a boundary stone or similar landmark with criminal intent, thus damning the soul to haunt the very boundary it unlawfully changed in life.

claims.statement: The Feuermann appears only in the evening or at night, preferably in fields, especially field borders, and meadows, particularly swampy ones.
claims.statement_id: Feuermann hanya muncul pada sore atau malam hari, terutama di ladang, khususnya batas ladang, dan padang rumput, terutama yang berawa.
claims.quote: The Feuermann appears only at evening or at night, preferably at fields, particularly field borders, and meadows, especially swampy ones.

claims.statement: The Feuerputz, also called Brünnling, Feuerpütz, Glühender, Züsler, but most often Feuermann, is a fiery spook and legendary figure.
claims.statement_id: Feuerputz, juga disebut Brünnling, Feuerpütz, Glühender, Züsler, tetapi paling sering Feuermann, adalah hantu berapi dan tokoh legenda.
claims.quote: Der Feuerputz, der auch Brünnling, Feuerpütz, Feurputz, Glühender, Züsler, am häufigsten aber Feuermann genannt wird, ist ein feuriger Spuk und eine Sagengestalt.

claims.statement: Feuermänner are souls who sinned in life and must now atone; their fiery form is their purgatory.
claims.statement_id: Feuermänner adalah jiwa yang berdosa semasa hidup dan kini harus menebusnya; wujud berapi mereka adalah api penyucian mereka.
claims.quote: Feuermänner sind Seelen, die sich im Leben versündigt haben und dies nun abbüßen müssen. Ihre feurige Erscheinung ist also ihr Fegefeuer.

claims.statement: Usually harmless, the Feuermann may help by lighting the way at night for a small coin or thanks such as 'Vergelt's Gott'; such a blessing redeems the burning sinner.
claims.statement_id: Biasanya tak berbahaya, Feuermann bisa menolong dengan menerangi jalan pada malam hari demi sedikit uang atau ucapan terima kasih seperti "Vergelt's Gott" ("semoga Tuhan membalasnya"); berkat semacam itu menebus pendosa yang terbakar itu.
claims.quote: Usually harmless, the Feuermann can also appear helpful to humans by showing and illuminating them the way at night for a small sum of money or a word of gratitude such as "Vergelt's Gott" ("May God reward it") or "Bezahl dir's Gott (soviel Mal wie du's nötig hast)" ("May God repay you (as many times as you need)"). Such a blessing redeems the burning sinner

claims.statement: A Feuermann turns malicious when refused a promised reward or taking revenge on a prankster; then it leads people astray and leaps onto their backs (aufhocken).
claims.statement_id: Feuermann menjadi jahat bila imbalan yang dijanjikan tidak diberikan atau bila membalas orang yang mempermainkannya; ia lalu menyesatkan orang dan melompat ke punggung mereka (aufhocken).
claims.quote: A malicious Feuermann can be experienced when it has helped out a human and is refused the promised reward or when it takes revenge on a human who has played a prank on it. Then, the Feuermann leads astray, practices "aufhocken"

claims.statement: Touching the Feuermann's hand is dangerous; so one should offer an object instead of one's hand, as a black handprint will be burnt where it touched.
claims.statement_id: Menyentuh tangan Feuermann berbahaya; karena itu orang sebaiknya menyodorkan benda alih-alih tangannya, sebab akan tertinggal cap tangan hitam yang terbakar di tempat yang disentuhnya.
claims.quote: It is dangerous to touch the Feuermann's hand. Thus, one should always give an object instead of one's hand as one will find a black handprint burnt on it where the Feuermann has touched.

claims.statement: A simple 'Vergelt's Gott' is said to be enough to redeem the Feuermann.
claims.statement_id: Ucapan sederhana "Vergelt's Gott" konon sudah cukup untuk menebus Feuermann.
claims.quote: Schon ein schlichtes „Vergelt's Gott“ soll dabei ausreichen, um den Feuermann zu erlösen.

claims.statement: Rarer forms are a fiery, sometimes headless rider on a fiery horse and a fiery ploughman with fiery horse and plough.
claims.statement_id: Penampakan yang lebih jarang adalah penunggang berapi, kadang tanpa kepala, di atas kuda berapi, dan pembajak berapi dengan kuda dan bajak berapi.
claims.quote: Rarer appearances are that of a fiery, sometimes headless rider on a fiery horse and that of a fiery ploughman with fiery horse and plough.

claims.statement: Such a blessing redeems the burning sinner, as do prayers and masses, so Feuermänner approach on hearing a prayer; swearing drives them away.
claims.statement_id: Berkat semacam itu menebus pendosa yang terbakar, begitu pula doa dan misa, sehingga Feuermänner mendekat bila mendengar doa; sebaliknya umpatan mengusir mereka.
claims.quote: Such a blessing redeems the burning sinner, as do prayers and masses because of which Feuermänner draw near upon hearing a prayer. Swearing drives them away instead.

claims.statement: Or it follows the person and sets the straw on their wagon or even their house on fire.

description.en: Fionn mac Cumhaill (alternatively spelled Finn mac Cumhaill), sometimes anglicised Finn McCool or MacCool, is a hero in Irish mythology, as well as in later Scottish and Manx folklore. He is the leader of the Fianna bands of young roving hunter-warriors, as well as being a seer and poet. He is said to have a magic thumb that bestows him with great wisdom. He is often depicted hunting with his hounds Bran and Sceólang, and fighting with his spear and sword. The tales of Fionn and his fiann form the Fianna Cycle or Fenian Cycle (an Fhiannaíocht), much of it narrated by Fionn's son, the poet Oisín; it has become the most important part of the c. 12th-century narrative Acallam na Senórach, and has also been told in other ancient Irish texts.

description.en: Firefox (tulikettu or tulirepo or tulikko) is a mythical creature in the folklore of northern and eastern Finland. It is a fox whose tail twinkles fire. According to folk stories, the Firefox lives far away in hideouts in the woods, or in the north, and very few are said to have seen it. Firefox is black during days but twinkles fire during nights. When Firefox's skin is brushed in a right manner it glitters strange light. According to stories, the leather of a Firefox has been used to illuminate powder storages at nights instead of dangerous open fire. The leather of a Firefox has been considered as immensely valuable. Hunters dream of the Firefox, since it has been said that catching it makes the hunter rich for the rest of his life. Firefox has given its name for northern lights which are called "fox's fires" (revontulet) in the Finnish language. In Lapland it has been told that the Firefox causes the northern lights with its tail which flings sparks when it touches low hanging branches or bushes while the fox is running. On December 12, 2025, NASA published a photograph of a wild fox under the northern lights as their Astronomy Picture of the Day, taken by photographer Dennis Lehtonen in Kilpisjärvi, Finland, and referencing Finnish mythology in the description.

description.en: Flogdrake (Old Swedish: floghdraki, flughdraki; Finnish: louhikäärme), also elddrake or eldsdrake (lit. 'fire dragon, fiery dragon'), dialectally also godsdrake (Dalecarlian: gussdratji, lit. 'goods dragon'), is a type of dragon in Swedish folklore, and to a lesser extent Finnish and Estonian folklore (see kratt), by analogy a variation of the Pan-European firedrake myth; it is a wingless worm-dragon that flies across the sky while glowing, looking like a streak of fire or light akin to a shooting star, while living in mountain tunnels that it bores. Related myths also exist in Northern Germany, for example the Schrat.

description.id: Empat Simbol (Inggris: Four Symbols; Hanzi: 四象; Pinyin: Sì Xiàng) adalah empat makhluk dalam mitologi Tiongkok pada rasi bintang Tiongkok. Empat Simbol tersebut adalah: Naga Biru di Timur (青龍) Burung Merah di Selatan (朱雀) Harimau Putih di Barat (白虎) Kura-kura Hitam di Utara (玄武) Masing-masing merepresentasikan arah dan musim pada suatu tahun dan mempunyai karakter tersendiri. Mereka menggambarkan mitologi Tiongkok, Korea serta Jepang Empat Simbol ini menjadi populer seiring dengan menyebarnya ajaran Taoisme. Naga Biru memiliki nama Meng Zhang (孟章), Burung Merah memiliki nama Ling Guang (陵光), Harimau Putih memiliki nama Jian Bing (監兵) dan Kura-kura Hitam memiliki nama Zhi Ming (執明).
description.en: The Four Symbols are mythological creatures appearing among the Chinese constellations along the ecliptic, and viewed as the guardians of the four cardinal directions. These four creatures are also referred to by a variety of other names, including "Four Guardians", "Four Gods", and "Four Auspicious Beasts". They are the Azure Dragon of the East, the Vermilion Bird of the South, the White Tiger of the West, and the Black Turtle-Snake (also called "Black Warrior") of the North. Each of the creatures is most closely associated with a cardinal direction and a color, but also additionally represents other aspects, including a season of the year, an emotion, virtue, and one of the Chinese "five elements" (wood, fire, metal, and water; earth is excluded, instead being represented by the Yellow Dragon). Each has been given its own individual traits, origin story and a reason for being. Symbolically, and as part of spiritual and religious belief and meaning, these creatures have been culturally important across countries in the Sinosphere.

description.en: A fuath (Scottish Gaelic: fuath; Scottish Gaelic pronunciation: [fuə]; lit. ‘hatred'; plural: fuathan; phonetic English: vough, vaugh) is a class of malevolent spirits in Scottish Highland folklore and Irish Folklore especially water spirits. In Sutherland was the so-called Moulin na Vaugha/Fouadh, ‘Mill of the Fuath', haunted by the fuath and her son, the amorphous brollachan. The mill was along a stream off Loch Migdale, and belonged to the Dempster family (Skibo Castle) estate. A fuath once seen at this mill was a nose-less banshee with yellow hair wearing a green silk dress; in the story of its capture it was tormented into submission by use of steel (awl, and more effectively by a sewing needle), but it turned to a jellyfish-like mass when light was shone on it. A fuath on the estate farm, encountered on a different occasion, had webbed feet. They sometimes reputedly intermarry with human beings (typically the female), whose offspring develop a mane and tail.

description.id: Gagoze (Jepang: 元興寺), juga memiliki sebutan lain Gangōji no Oni, Gagoji, Guwagoze, atau Gangō adalah salah satu yokai yang berwujud hantu iblis. Menurut cerita rakyat Jepang, cerita tentang yokai ini muncul berabad-abad yang lalu di Gangō-ji, sebuah kuil di Nara. Ia dideskripsikan sebagai iblis mengerikan yang mengenakan jubah biarawan dan merangkak dengan keempat kakinya. Legendanya disimpan di Kuil Gangō yang didirikan pada tahun 593 oleh Soga no Umako. Gagoze dahulunya merupakan seorang pelayan kuil dengan kepribadiannya yang malas dan jahat. Kisah hantu Gagoze berasal dari teks abad ke-9 yang berjudul Nihon Ryoiki (Catatan Kejadian Hantu Aneh di Jepang).
description.en: Gagoze (元興寺), also gagoji, guwagoze, gangō, and gangōji no oni (元興寺の鬼, the oni of gangōji) is a yōkai said to have appeared at Gangō-ji in the Nara Prefecture around the Asuka period. It can also be found in the text of the Heian period Nihon Ryōiki (in the story, 雷の憙を得て生ま令めし子の強き力在る縁," On a Boy of Great Strength Who Was Born of the Thunder’s Rejoicing"), the Honchō Monzui, among others. In classical yōkai drawings such as the Gazu Hyakki Yagyō by Toriyama Sekien, it is depicted as an oni with the appearance of a monk.

description.id: Gandaberunda (Dewanagari: गण्डभेरुण्ड; ,IAST: Gaṇḍabheruṇḍa,; arti: berleher hebat) atau Berunda (Dewanagari: भेरुण्ड; ,IAST: Bheruṇḍa,; arti: dahsyat) adalah burung berleher dua dalam mitologi Hindu, yang merupakan salah satu penjelmaan Wisnu. Menurut mitologi Hindu, ia memiliki kekuatan gaib yang sangat besar. Menurut aliran Waisnawa, ia dihormati sebagai salah satu wujud Wisnu yang dipakai untuk bertarung dan menaklukkan Saraba (dalam kepercayaan Saiwa, Saraba adalah wujud yang diambil oleh Siwa untuk menenangkan Narasinga).
description.en: Gandabherunda (IAST: Gaṇḍabheruṇḍa) is a form of Vishnu in Hindu mythology. According to legend, Narasimha, an avatar of Vishnu, assumes this form of a double-headed eagle to subdue Sharabha, a form of Shiva. Gandabherunda is worshipped along with his consort Narasimhi, a fierce form of Lakshmi, also revered as Simhamukhi Lakshmi.

description.en: Gangcheori (강철이; 強鐵) is a dragon-shaped monster in Korean mythology that was introduced in the 17th century. It is a monster that has traditionally been popular throughout the country. It also has been called Gangcheol (강철), Kkangcheol (깡철), and Ggoangcheol (꽝철). One of the earliest records of Gangcheori being mentioned is the Jibong Yuseol (1614). In those days, there was an old saying, "Where Gangcheori goes it is like spring, even if it is fall." When author Lee Soo-kwang asked an old man in the countryside about the origin of the word, the old man told him about a monster called Gangcheori that burns down everything in a few miles.

description.id: Ghoul adalah mayat hidup atau roh jahat dalam mitologi Arab. Istilah ini pertama kali digunakan dalam literatur bahasa Inggris pada tahun 1786, pada novel orientalisme karya William Beckford yang berjudul Vathek.
description.en: In folklore, a ghoul (from Arabic: غول, ghūl) is a demon-like being or monstrous humanoid, often associated with graveyards and the consumption of human flesh. The concept of the ghoul originated in pre-Islamic Arabian religion. Modern fiction often uses the term to label a specific kind of monster. By extension, the word "ghoul" is also used in a derogatory sense to refer to a person who delights in the macabre or whose occupation directly involves death, such as a gravedigger or mortician.

description.en: In Nordic folklore; Danish: genganger, Norwegian: gjenganger, Swedish: gengångare ("(a)gain-walker"), among more, is a term for a revenant or ghost, meaning "someone which goes again", from the Scandinavian verb of "going again" (Norwegian: gå igjen, Swedish: gå igen), in the sense of a deceased walking beyond the grave, haunting post-mortem; compare German: Wiedergänger ("Re-walker"). Other forms includes Icelandic: afturganga, Norwegian: attergangar, stemming from Old Norse: aptrgangr ("re-walker"); Danish: genfærd, Norwegian: gjenferd ("again-travel or after-journey").

description.id: Goblin adalah sejenis makhluk supranatural yang muncul dalam dongeng-dongeng dan kisah-kisah fiksi fantasi. Mereka memiliki tinggi berkisar antara 30 cm sampai dengan 2 m. Biasanya kulit mereka berwarna hijau seperti daun. Dalam cerita rakyat Eropa, Goblin merupakan bangsa peri atau makhluk supranatural. Ukuran tubuh mereka kecil dan kadang kala tidak terlihat oleh mata manusia. Mereka dilukiskan sebagai makhluk mungil berwarna hijau dan bertelinga runcing. Goblin juga digambarkan sebagai makhluk aneh kerdil, nakal, bahkan terkadang jahat. Mereka dikaitkan dengan berbagai kemampuan, temperamen dan penampilan yang semuanya tergantung pada cerita dan negara asal. Dalam beberapa kasus, Goblin telah diklasifikasikan sebagai makhluk kecil yang terus-menerus mengganggu dan memiliki berbagai kemampuan magis. Mereka juga sangat serakah dan cinta emas atau jenis perhiasan. Goblin juga erat kaitannya dengan api dan memiliki kemahiran untuk menciptakannya. Menurut versi lain dalam beberapa dongeng dan kisah fantasi, Goblin merupakan bangsa makhluk yang buas dan ganas. Mereka tinggal di gua-gua yang gelap atau di bawah tanah. Ras mereka diidentikkan dengan makhluk jahat dan merupakan petarung yang brutal. Mereka dilukiskan sebagai makhluk berbadan tegap seperti manusia, berkulit hijau, telinganya lancip, dan berwajah sangar dan mengerikan. Kadang-kadang mereka menculik bayi dan memangsa manusia. Kadang kala Goblin juga memiliki keahlian dalam kegiatan perniagaan dan keuangan. Dalam kisah Harry Potter, Goblin memiliki kecakapan dalam perbankan dan dalam game World of Warcraft mereka memiliki keahlian dalam menjual rumah. Ada juga yang beranggapan Goblin adalah makhluk bijaksana.
description.en: A goblin is a diminutive, grotesque, and often malevolent humanoid creature prominent in European folklore, typically characterized by its mischievous or demonic nature, small stature (around 30 cm (12 in) in some traditions), furry or leathery appearance, and ability to shapeshift. Goblins are believed to dwell in subterranean areas or households, where they engage in acts ranging from pranks to murder. Their etymology derives from Old French gobelin (late 12th century), possibly linked to Medieval Latin gobelinus or Greek kobalos (meaning rogue or sprite), though some scholars trace it to earlier domestic protector spirits like the Germanic kobold, which were later demonized under Christian influence. Similar creatures include brownies, dwarves, duendes, gnomes, imps, leprechauns, and kobolds, but it is also commonly used as a blanket term for all small, fay creatures. The term is sometimes expanded to include goblin-like creatures of other cultures, such as the pukwudgie, dokkaebi, or ifrit.

This French form traces back to Medieval Latin gobelinus, appearing around 1140 in Orderic Vitalis's Historia ecclesiastica, referring to a demon expelled from a church in Évreux.

claims.statement: The Welsh coblyn, a knocker, derives from Old French gobelin via English goblin.
claims.statement_id: Kata Wales (Welsh) coblyn, sejenis knocker, berasal dari gobelin (Old French) melalui goblin (English).
claims.quote: The Welsh coblyn, a type of knocker, derives from the Old French gobelin via the English goblin.

claims.statement: In English and Scottish folklore goblins appear as brownies, household spirits doing night chores for an offering of porridge or milk.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Inggris dan Skotlandia (English, Scottish), goblin muncul sebagai brownie, roh rumah yang mengerjakan tugas malam hari bila diberi bubur (porridge) atau susu (milk).
claims.quote: In English and Scottish folklore, goblins often appear as brownies, benevolent household spirits that perform domestic chores such as threshing grain, churning butter, or tending livestock during the night, provided they receive a small offering like porridge or milk left by the hearth.

claims.statement: In contrast, boggarts from Yorkshire are a more malevolent variant.
claims.statement_id: Sebaliknya, boggart dari Yorkshire adalah varian yang lebih jahat (malevolent).
claims.quote: In contrast, boggarts from Yorkshire traditions represent a more malevolent variant

claims.statement: Similar creatures include brownies, dwarves, duendes, gnomes, imps, leprechauns and kobolds; it is also a blanket term for all small fay creatures.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk serupa goblin: brownie, kurcaci, duende, gnome, imp, leprechaun, kobold; kata ini juga sebutan umum (blanket term) semua makhluk peri kecil.
claims.quote: Similar creatures include brownies, dwarves, duendes, gnomes, imps, leprechauns, and kobolds, but it is also commonly used as a blanket term for all small, fay creatures.

claims.statement: The term goblin entered English in the early 14th century from Old French gobelin.
claims.statement_id: Kata goblin masuk ke bahasa Inggris (English) awal abad ke-14 dari gobelin bahasa Prancis Kuno (Old French).
claims.quote: The term "goblin" entered English in the early 14th century, derived from the Anglo-Norman French gobelin or Old French gobelin

claims.statement: In European (Eropa) folklore Goblins are fairy folk (bangsa peri), small, sometimes unseen, little green beings with pointed ears (telinga runcing).
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Eropa, Goblin bangsa peri, kecil, kadang tak terlihat, mungil berwarna hijau dan bertelinga runcing.
claims.quote: Dalam cerita rakyat Eropa, Goblin merupakan bangsa peri atau makhluk supranatural. Ukuran tubuh mereka kecil dan kadang kala tidak terlihat oleh mata manusia. Mereka dilukiskan sebagai makhluk mungil berwarna hijau dan bertelinga runcing.

claims.statement: Goblins are greedy and love gold (emas), are tied to fire (api), and in other versions are savage (buas), living in dark caves (gua-gua) or underground.
claims.statement_id: Goblin serakah dan cinta emas, terkait api (api), dan menurut versi lain buas serta tinggal di gua-gua gelap atau bawah tanah.
claims.quote: Mereka juga sangat serakah dan cinta emas atau jenis perhiasan. Goblin juga erat kaitannya dengan api dan memiliki kemahiran untuk menciptakannya. Menurut versi lain dalam beberapa dongeng dan kisah fantasi, Goblin merupakan bangsa makhluk yang buas dan ganas. Mereka tinggal di gua-gua yang gelap atau di bawah tanah.

claims.statement: Scholars link it to Ancient Greek kóbalos ("rogue") and to the Germanic household spirit kobold.
claims.statement_id: Para sarjana mengaitkan goblin dengan kóbalos (Yunani Kuno, Ancient Greek, "rogue") dan dengan kobold, roh rumah Jermanik (Germanic).
claims.quote: Scholars propose possible etymological connections to earlier languages, including Ancient Greek kóbalos, meaning "rogue" or "mischievous sprite", which may have influenced post-classical Latin forms like cobalus denoting a demon. Additionally, links have been suggested to Germanic kobold, a household spirit

claims.statement: Goblins are sometimes classed as small pestering beings with various magical powers (kemampuan magis).
claims.statement_id: Goblin kadang diklasifikasikan sebagai makhluk kecil pengganggu dengan berbagai kemampuan magis (kemampuan magis).
claims.quote: Dalam beberapa kasus, Goblin telah diklasifikasikan sebagai makhluk kecil yang terus-menerus mengganggu dan memiliki berbagai kemampuan magis.

description.en: In Slovene folklore, Goldhorn or Goldenhorn (Slovene: Zlatorog) is a legendary white chamois buck, or alternatively, an Alpine ibex, that had his realm in the heights of Mount Triglav, the highest mountain in Slovenia and the highest peak of the Julian Alps. The legend is well known throughout Slovenia (specifically Carinthia), as well as in Austrian Carinthia, and Italian Friuli-Venezia Giulia. The story about Zlatorog was first written down, adapted to the late Romantic style and published by Karl Deschmann (Karel Dežman) in the Laibacher Zeitung, no. 43, on 21 February 1868.

claims.statement: Goldhorn is documented as goldhorn golden horns in regional lore.
claims.statement_id: Goldhorn adalah figur mitologis dalam catatan cerita rakyat.
claims.quote: Goldhorn's golden horns were the key to a treasure hidden in the mountains around Triglav.

description.en: The Gougou is one of the oldest Mi'kmaq legends in Canadian folklore. It is said to be ogress that lives on Miscou Island, located in northeast New Brunswick in the Gulf of St. Lawrence. It was mentioned by Samuel de Champlain when writing about his exploration of the area in 1603. William F. Ganong made attempts to uncover the legend when surveying the area in 1903.

claims.statement: The Gougou is one of the oldest Mi'kmaq legends in Canadian folklore.
claims.statement_id: Gougou adalah salah satu legenda Mi'kmaq tertua dalam cerita rakyat Kanada.
claims.quote: The Gougou is one of the oldest Mi'kmaq legends in Canadian folklore.

claims.statement: Described as an ogress residing on Miscou Island in northeastern New Brunswick.
claims.statement_id: Dikatakan sebagai raksasa wanita pemakan manusia yang tinggal di Pulau Miscou, New Brunswick.
claims.quote: It is said to be ogress that lives on Miscou Island, located in northeast New Brunswick in the Gulf of St. Lawrence.

claims.statement: Mentioned by explorer Samuel de Champlain during his regional exploration in 1603.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini disebutkan oleh Samuel de Champlain dalam catatan penjelajahannya tahun 1603.
claims.quote: It was mentioned by Samuel de Champlain when writing about his exploration of the area in 1603.

description.en: In French folklore, Graoully (spelled as Graouli, Graouilly, Graouille or Graully) is a creature with the appearance of a dragon. According to legend, it lived in the arena of the Roman amphitheater in Metz, France. Legends state that Saint Clement of Metz fought against Graoully and vanquished the beast.

claims.statement: In French folklore Graoully (also Graouli, Graouilly, Graouille or Graully) is a dragon-like creature that by legend lived in the arena of the Roman amphitheatre at Metz, and Saint Clement of Metz fought and overcame it.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Prancis, Graoully (juga Graouli, Graouilly, Graouille, atau Graully) adalah makhluk berwujud naga yang menurut legenda tinggal di arena amfiteater Romawi di Metz, dan Santo Klemens dari Metz melawan serta mengalahkannya.
claims.quote: In French folklore, Graoully (spelled as Graouli, Graouilly, Graouille or Graully) is a creature with the appearance of a dragon. According to legend, it lived in the arena of the Roman amphitheater in Metz, France. Legends state that Saint Clement of Metz fought against Graoully and vanquished the beast.

claims.statement: Serpents in the amphitheatre poisoned the air with their venomous breath and so barred access to the city.
claims.statement_id: Ular-ular di amfiteater meracuni udara dengan napas berbisa sehingga orang tidak bisa memasuki kota.
claims.quote: Mais des serpents installés dans l'amphithéâtre empoisonnent l'air de leur souffle venimeux et interdisent ainsi l'accès à la ville.

claims.statement: The bishop went to the serpents' pit, raised his cross, caught Graoully with his stole, and led the dragon away until it vanished across the River Seille with the other serpents.
claims.statement_id: Sang uskup pergi ke sarang ular, mengangkat salibnya, menangkap Graoully dengan stolanya, lalu menuntun naga itu pergi hingga lenyap di seberang Sungai Seille bersama ular-ular lainnya.
claims.quote: The bishop went to the serpents pit, held up his cross and captured Le Graoully with his stole – the long wide band worn over the shoulders. He then led the dragon away and made sure it disappeared over the Seille River along with the rest of the serpents.

claims.statement: In many depictions and versions, however, Saint Clement instead killed the dragon by piercing it with a polearm.
claims.statement_id: Namun dalam banyak gambaran dan versi, Santo Klemens justru membunuh naga itu dengan menusuknya memakai tombak bergagang panjang.
claims.quote: However, in many depictions and versions of the story, Saint Clément instead slew the dragon by piercing it with a polearm.

claims.statement: According to the German article, on an island in the Seille the monster was swallowed by the earth, and Clement sealed the hole with a rock said still to be visible.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, di sebuah pulau di Seille monster itu ditelan bumi, dan Klemens menutup lubangnya dengan batu yang konon masih terlihat sampai kini.
claims.quote: Dort wurde das Ungeheuer vom Erdboden verschluckt. Clemens verschloss das Loch mit einem Felsen, der angeblich noch heute zu sehen ist.

claims.statement: The word Graoully is believed to come from French grouiller, 'to swarm'.
claims.statement_id: Kata Graoully diyakini berasal dari kata Prancis grouiller, "berkerumun".
claims.quote: It is believed that the word Graoully derives from the French word "grouiller" meaning "swarm".

claims.statement: The German article says the name may come from gräulich, 'horrible'.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Jerman menyebut namanya mungkin dari kata gräulich, "mengerikan".
claims.quote: Der Name soll sich von „gräulich“ (schrecklich) ableiten.

claims.statement: The first version of the legend of Saint Clement of Metz dates from the late 10th century.
claims.statement_id: Versi pertama legenda Santo Klemens dari Metz berasal dari akhir abad ke-10.
claims.quote: La première version de la légende de Saint Clément de Metz date de la fin du Xe siècle.

claims.statement: The legend symbolises the destruction of pagan religions, traditionally shown as serpent and dragon, and their replacement by Christianity.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini melambangkan hancurnya agama pagan, yang biasa digambarkan sebagai ular dan naga, dan penggantiannya oleh agama Kristen.
claims.quote: Cette légende représente symboliquement la destruction des religions païennes — traditionnellement représentées par la figure du serpent et du dragon — et leur remplacement par le christianisme.

claims.statement: A procession with an effigy of the dragon was held in the city until the 19th century.
claims.statement_id: Prosesi dengan patung naga itu diadakan di kota sampai abad ke-19.
claims.quote: A procession with an effigy of the dragon was held in the city until the nineteenth century.

claims.statement: The name of the Rue Taison near the cathedral is traced to a warning about Graoully: 'Taisons, taisons nous, voilà le Graoully qui passe' (hush, the Graoully is passing).
claims.statement_id: Nama Rue Taison dekat katedral konon berasal dari peringatan tentang Graoully: "Taisons, taisons nous, voilà le Graoully qui passe" (diamlah, Graoully sedang lewat).
claims.quote: Der Name der Rue Taison, einer Straße unweit der Kathedrale, wird auf eine Warnung vor dem Graoully zurückgeführt: „Taisons, taisons nous, voilà le Graoully qui passe“

claims.statement: A figure of Graoully is in the cathedral crypt, a copy hangs in a hall of the Hohkönigsburg, and until 2021 the beast featured on the crest of FC Metz.
claims.statement_id: Patung Graoully ada di kripta katedral Metz, salinannya tergantung di Hohkönigsburg, dan sampai 2021 makhluk ini muncul di lambang klub sepak bola FC Metz.
claims.quote: Eine Figur des Graoully befindet sich in der Krypta der Kathedrale; eine Kopie davon hängt in einem Saal der Hohkönigsburg. Bis 2021 war das Fabeltier auch auf dem Wappen des Fußballclubs FC Metz zu sehen.

description.en: The Grootslang or Grote Slang (Afrikaans and Dutch for "big snake") is a legendary creature that is reputed to dwell in a deep cave in the Richtersveld, South Africa.

claims.statement: The Grootslang is a legendary creature reputed to dwell in a deep cave in the Richtersveld, South Africa.
claims.statement_id: Grootslang berarti ular besar dalam bahasa Afrikaans dan Belanda, makhluk legendaris di gua Richtersveld, Afrika Selatan.
claims.quote: The Grootslang or Grote Slang (Afrikaans and Dutch for "big snake") is a legendary creature that is reputed to dwell in a deep cave in the Richtersveld, South Africa.

claims.statement: The Grootslang is described as being 40 to 50 feet (12 to 15 m) in length.
claims.statement_id: Grootslang digambarkan memiliki panjang 12 hingga 15 meter.
claims.quote: The Grootslang is described as being 40–50 feet (12–15 m) in length, and to leave a track 3 feet (0.91 m) wide.

claims.statement: Some legends describe it as having diamonds in its eye sockets.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian legenda menggambarkannya memiliki intan di rongga matanya.
claims.quote: Some legends describe it as having diamonds in its eye sockets.

claims.statement: The Grootslang is said to dwell in a cave known as the Wonder Hole or Bottomless Pit in the Richtersveld.
claims.statement_id: Grootslang menghuni gua yang dikenal sebagai Wonder Hole atau Bottomless Pit di Richtersveld.
claims.quote: The Grootslang is said to be a huge serpent that dwells in a cave known as the "Wonder Hole" or the "Bottomless Pit" located in the Richtersveld, which is said to connect to the sea 64 kilometres (40 mi) away.

claims.statement: Known as the Great Snake of the Orange River in South Africa.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini juga dikenal sebagai Great Snake of the Orange River di Afrika Selatan.
claims.quote: Creature information Other name Great Snake of the Orange River Grouping Legendary creature Sub grouping Reptiles, Serpents and Worms Similar entities Irizima, Mokele-mbembe Origin Country South Africa Region Richtersveld Details Caves, rivers

description.en: Guaraci or Quaraci (from Tupi kûarasý, "sun") in the Guaraní mythology is the god of the Sun, creator of all living creatures.

claims.statement: Guaraci or Quaraci (from Tupi kûarasý, "sun") is the Sun god of Guaraní mythology, creator of all living creatures.
claims.statement_id: Guaraci atau Quaraci (dari kata Tupi kûarasý, "matahari") adalah dewa Matahari dalam mitologi Guaraní, pencipta semua makhluk hidup.
claims.quote: Guaraci or Quaraci (from Tupi kûarasý, "sun") in the Guaraní mythology is the god of the Sun, creator of all living creatures.

description.en: Guivre (or givre) and vouivre are French names for a type of serpentine mythical creature, by extension a dragon, by some accords, equivalent to a lindworm or wyvern. The names can be used synonymously for the same creature, the former deriving from the latter, or refer to different but similar mythological creatures depending on the myth. In legend they are portrayed as serpentine creatures who possessed venomous breath and prowled the countryside of Medieval France.

claims.statement: Guivre (or givre) and vouivre are French names for a serpentine mythical creature, by extension a dragon, by some accounts equivalent to a lindworm or wyvern.
claims.statement_id: Guivre (atau givre) dan vouivre adalah nama Prancis untuk sejenis makhluk mitis berwujud ular, lebih luas lagi naga, yang menurut sebagian pihak setara dengan lindworm atau wyvern.
claims.quote: Guivre (or givre) and vouivre are French names for a type of serpentine mythical creature, by extension a dragon, by some accords, equivalent to a lindworm or wyvern.

claims.statement: In legend they are serpentine creatures with venomous breath that prowled the countryside of medieval France.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda mereka digambarkan sebagai makhluk mirip ular bernapas racun yang berkeliaran di pedesaan Prancis abad pertengahan.
claims.quote: In legend they are portrayed as serpentine creatures who possessed venomous breath and prowled the countryside of Medieval France.

claims.statement: The English word wyvern derives from Old French vouivre.
claims.statement_id: Kata Inggris wyvern berasal dari kata Prancis Kuno vouivre.
claims.quote: The English wyvern (a type of dragon) derives from Old French "vouivre".

claims.statement: Guivres had a long serpentine body and a dragon's head, hind feet barely visible if present at all, and in some accounts horns on the forehead.
claims.statement_id: Guivre bertubuh panjang seperti ular dan berkepala naga, kaki belakangnya hampir tak terlihat kalaupun ada, dan dalam sebagian kisah bertanduk di dahi.
claims.quote: Guivres (alternatively givres) were said to possess a long, serpentine body and a dragon's head. The hind feet are not as visible if present at all. The guivre had horns in its forehead in some accounts, as well.

claims.statement: Locally in France it was known as extremely aggressive, sometimes attacking unprovoked, yet it feared naked humans and would blush and look away on seeing one.
claims.statement_id: Di Prancis ia dikenal sangat agresif dan kadang menyerang tanpa sebab, tetapi takut pada manusia telanjang: bila melihatnya, guivre tersipu dan memalingkan muka.
claims.quote: Locally in France, it was known as an extremely aggressive creature that would sometimes attack without being provoked. They were afraid of naked humans, and when saw them, blushed and looked away.

claims.statement: Guivres lived in small bodies of water like pools and lakes, in forests and in any damp place.
claims.statement_id: Guivre tinggal di perairan kecil seperti kolam dan danau, di hutan, dan di tempat lembap.
claims.quote: Documentation points to their residence as being in small bodies of water like pools and lakes, forests, and any damp place.

claims.statement: Samson of Dol witnessed an encounter between a priest and a small dragon-like creature called La Guivre.
claims.statement_id: Santo Samson dari Dol menyaksikan pertemuan seorang imam dengan makhluk kecil mirip naga yang disebut La Guivre.
claims.quote: Samson of Dol was present at an encounter between a small dragon-like creature, known as La Guivre ("the guivre"), and a priest.

claims.statement: Saint Suliao rebuked the priest who had hidden bread in his robe, pulled a hideous serpentine creature from it, exorcised it and had another man throw it from a roof in Garot.
claims.statement_id: Santo Suliao menegur imam yang menyembunyikan roti di jubahnya, mengeluarkan makhluk ular yang mengerikan dari jubah itu, mengusirnya, lalu menyuruh orang lain melemparkannya dari atap sebuah bangunan di Garot.
claims.quote: He admonished the priest and removed a hideous serpentine creature from the robe. There, he exorcised it and then compelled another man to throw it from the roof of a building in Garot.

claims.statement: According to the French article, the vouivre is a legendary creature of several European countries, usually a two-legged dragon or winged serpent often bearing a carbuncle on its brow, called guivre in heraldry.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, vouivre adalah makhluk legenda di beberapa negara Eropa, biasanya berupa naga berkaki dua atau ular bersayap yang sering membawa batu merah delima di dahinya, dan dalam heraldik disebut guivre.
claims.quote: La vouivre est une créature légendaire présente dans plusieurs pays européens, ayant généralement la forme d'un dragon bipède ou d'un serpent ailé. Elle est souvent censée porter une escarboucle sur le front. En héraldique, elle est aussi appelée guivre.

claims.statement: The word vouivre is a regionalism of Lorraine, Burgundy, Franche-Comté, the Jura and Switzerland.
claims.statement_id: Kata vouivre adalah regionalisme khas Lorraine, Bourgogne, Franche-Comté, Jura, dan Swiss.
claims.quote: Ce mot est un régionalisme linguistique propre à la Lorraine, la Bourgogne, la Franche-Comté, le Jura et la Suisse.

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, all these forms ultimately come from Latin vipera, like Spanish víbora.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, semua bentuk ini akhirnya berasal dari kata Latin vipera, seperti kata Spanyol víbora.
claims.quote: Todas estas formas se derivan en última instancia del latín Vipera, como es el Español víbora.

description.id: Gwishin (Hangul: 귀신; RR: Gwishin) adalah hantu atau arwah dalam mitologi Korea. Mereka dianggap mirip dengan Yogoi (bahasa Korea: 요괴); dan Mamul (bahasa Korea: 마물). Mereka adalah manusia yang sudah mati, dan bukan sejenis monster. Dalam cerita rakyat Korea, Gwishin sering di bangunan, rumah, kuburan, hutan, dan sekolah yang ditinggalkan. Ketika seseorang meninggal tanpa menyelesaikan tugas yang harus mereka lakukan, roh mereka tetap berada di bumi untuk menyelesaikan tugas sebelum melanjutkan ke dunia bawah. Namun, Gwishin yang sangat kuat tidak pergi ke dunia bawah tanah jika mereka ingin tetap tinggal di bumi.
description.en: In Korean folklore, Gwisin (Korean: 귀신) are a type of deity, divinity, spirit or ghost. They are considered similar to a yogoe (Korean: 요괴) or mamul (Korean: 마물). Unlike dokkaebi, gwisin are humans who have died. According to folklore, gwisin may be found in many places. It is claimed that when an individual dies but still has ties to the world of the living, such as in the case of revenge or caring for a loved one, their spirit remains on earth to complete the task before going on to the underworld.

claims.statement: Gwisin are spirits of dead people in Korean folklore, distinct from dokkaebi.
claims.statement_id: Gwisin adalah roh orang mati dalam cerita rakyat Korea, berbeda dari dokkaebi.
claims.quote: In Korean folklore, Gwisin (Korean: 귀신) are a type of deity, divinity, spirit or ghost. They are considered similar to a yogoe (Korean: 요괴) or mamul (Korean: 마물). Unlike dokkaebi, gwisin are humans who have died.

claims.statement: Ties to the living, such as revenge or care for loved ones, may keep a spirit on earth.
claims.statement_id: Ikatan dengan dunia hidup, seperti balas dendam atau menjaga orang tersayang, dapat menahan roh di bumi.
claims.quote: According to folklore, gwisin may be found in many places. It is claimed that when an individual dies but still has ties to the world of the living, such as in the case of revenge or caring for a loved one, their spirit remains on earth to complete the task before going on to the underworld.

claims.statement: Revenge is a common theme in gwisin tales.
claims.statement_id: Balas dendam menjadi tema umum cerita tentang gwisin.
claims.quote: There are a lot of legends about gwisin. Because they are a common form of ghost, children often make them up to scare others or parents tell stories to their children to teach them a lesson. The most common plot of a legend about gwisin is revenge, for example revenge for the family of the ghost. Another popular trope includes men who cheat on their wives, and murder someone.

claims.statement: Cheonyeo-gwisin is the spirit of a woman who died unmarried.
claims.statement_id: Cheonyeo-gwisin adalah roh perempuan yang meninggal tanpa menikah.
claims.quote: The Cheonyeo-gwisin (처녀귀신) is the gwisin of a woman who died unmarried and usually have white Hanbok (한복) which are worn for funerals.

claims.statement: Mul-gwisin is the spirit of a drowned person.
claims.statement_id: Mul-gwisin adalah roh orang yang tenggelam.
claims.quote: The Mul-gwisin (물귀신) is the spirit of someone who drowned.

description.en: Habetrot (Habitrot, Habtrot and Habbitrot) is a figure in folklore of the Border counties of Northern England and Lowland Scotland, associated with spinning and the spinning wheel.

claims.statement: Habetrot (Habitrot, Habtrot, Habbitrot), a folklore figure of the Border counties of Northern England and Lowland Scotland, linked with spinning.
claims.statement_id: Habetrot (Habitrot, Habtrot, Habbitrot), tokoh folklor daerah perbatasan (Border) Inggris Utara (Northern England) dan Dataran Rendah Skotlandia (Lowland Scotland), terkait pemintalan.
claims.quote: Habetrot (Habitrot, Habtrot and Habbitrot) is a figure in folklore of the Border counties of Northern England and Lowland Scotland, associated with spinning and the spinning wheel.

claims.statement: A Selkirkshire tale of type ATU 501 (The Three Old Spinning Women); an old deformed woman living underground with other spinners.
claims.statement_id: Dongeng Selkirkshire, tipe ATU 501 (The Three Old Spinning Women); perempuan tua cacat yang tinggal di bawah tanah bersama pemintal lain.
claims.quote: Habetrot appears in a Selkirkshire folktale which is a variant of the Aarne–Thompson–Uther Index tale type ATU 501, "The Three Old Spinning Women". She is an old, deformed woman who lives underground with a group of other spinsters

claims.statement: Scantlie Mab; Habetrot spun for a girl and convinced her husband she should never spin again.
claims.statement_id: Scantlie Mab; Habetrot memintal untuk seorang gadis lalu meyakinkan suaminya agar ia tak memintal lagi.
claims.quote: The only other named spinster is Scantlie Mab. Habetrot spun yarn for a local girl and then convinced the girl's new husband that she should never spin again.

claims.statement: Similar tales in Germany (The Three Spinners) and Norway (The Three Aunts).
claims.statement_id: Kisah serupa di Jerman (Germany, The Three Spinners) dan Norwegia (Norway, The Three Aunts).
claims.quote: Similar tales appear in countries such as Germany (such as The Three Spinners) and Norway (The Three Aunts).

claims.statement: it article: Scantlie Mab; Habetrot spun for a local girl.
claims.statement_id: Artikel it: Scantlie Mab; Habetrot memintal untuk gadis setempat (Habetrot filava).
claims.quote: L'unica altra filatrice nominata è Scantlie Mab. Habetrot filava il filato per una ragazza del posto e poi convinse il nuovo marito della ragazza che non avrebbe mai più dovuto filare.

claims.statement: Grave-merels from unchristened graves is relieved only by a linen sack spun by Habetrot (Border lore).
claims.statement_id: Penyakit grave-merels dari makam bayi tak dibaptis hanya reda dengan karung linen yang dipintal Habetrot (Border).
claims.quote: The only way to relieve this was for the afflicted to wear a sack made from linen grown in a field using manure from a farmyard that has not been disturbed for forty years, spun by Habetrot

description.en: A hairen (海人, "sea-human") is a sea-dwelling human or humanoid in Chinese lore, also called kaijin (海人) by Japanese sources. According to a Chinese texts which were actually authored by Europeans, the hairen was human-like overall but possessed webbed feet and hands, and one was captured in Holland, who had loose drooping skin on her whole body, almost like she wore a piece of garment (specifically a paofu or long robe). This refers to the "marine woman" captured in 1403 (Mermaid of Edam) recorded in various sources, though Dutch sources said she was covered with some aquatic substance (later assumed to be sea moss or seaweed). The account of the "sea-humans" also recurred in Japanese sources dating to the Edo Period, such as Kaibara Ekken's Yamato honzō, which describe the creature as having skin that hangs down to the ground, like a pair of hakama trousers being worn.

description.en: In Finnish mythology, a haltija is a supernatural inhabitant of a specific place and a protector of living beings, living in an invisible environment but able to show themselves to humans. A haltija could be the supernatural original inhabitant and guardian of a place or the original mother of an animal species. A person who died and was buried to their home could also become a haltija. A haltija of a locality is a solitary creature who protects their home, its nature and peace. A haltija of an animal species protects their continued existence by returning dead animals back to earth. Deity-like figures in Finnish mythology are often described as jumala and/or haltija. Risto Pulkkinen described a jumala as a being who rules over a wider concept, such as water, while a haltija is more localized, ruling over a specific body of water. According to him, there is only a small number of beings in Finnish paganism which could be called jumala, but a wide variety of haltija beings. Thus, a haltija is a ruler of a domain smaller than a god's.

description.id: Dalam mitologi Sumeria dan Akkadia (serta mitologi Mesopotamia pada umumnya), Hanbi atau Hanpa (lebih umum dikenal dalam literatur Barat) adalah raja kejahatan, penguasa dari segala kekuatan jahat (Udug), dan ayah dari Pazuzu. Selain dari hubungannya dengan Pazuzu, sangat sedikit yang diketahui mengenai sosok ini. Beberapa pihak telah mengaitkan Hanbi dengan Helel, nama Yahudi yang secara umum disamakan dengan Lucifer dalam pemikiran Kristen. Namun, karakteristik Hanbi sebagai entitas bayangan yang lahir di dunia bawah, berbeda dengan dewa-dewa dunia bawah Sumeria (Dingir), membuatnya lebih mirip dengan konsep shedim dan se'iri dalam kepercayaan Yahudi atau syaitan dalam ajaran Islam.
description.en: In Sumerian and Akkadian mythology (and Mesopotamian mythology in general) Hanbi or Hanpa (more commonly known in western text) was the lord of evil, lord of all evil forces (Udug) and the father of Pazuzu. Aside from his relationship with Pazuzu, very little is known of this figure. Some have connected Hanbi to Helel, the Jewish name generally equated to Lucifer in Christian thought. However, Hanbi's characteristic of being a shadow born in the underworld, different from the Sumerian gods (Dingir) of the underworld, would make him more similar to the concept of the Jewish shedim and se'iri or the Islamic shaitan.

description.en: The Hemann (German: [ˈheːˌman]), also Homann, Hoymann, Hoimann, or Jochhoimann, (Mann = man), is a spirit from German folklore known to scare people through yelling, usually invisibly and at night. The first part of its name usually depicts the kind of yell heard from the Hemann. It can be found in former German-speaking Bohemia (where the Czechs also know it as Hejkadlo), former German-speaking Silesia, Upper Palatinate, the Fichtel Mountains, the Vogtland, Westphalia, and around Crailsheim in Baden-Württemberg.

description.en: Herensuge is the name for a mythical dragon in the Basque language. In Basque mythology, dragons appear sparingly, sometimes with seven heads. Herensuge often also appear in the form of a serpent. The seven heads were believed to be the offspring of the Herensuge dragon. When the little dragons were fully grown, they would fall off their mother's head. Only the god Sugaar is associated with this creature but more often with a serpent. A legend describes a Navarrese knight, Teodosio de Goñi, who while making penance for double parricide in the Aralar Range rescues a woman that had been given as ransom to the dragon. When the chains that tie his ankles are bitten by the dragon and he sees no way of defeating it, the knight prays to Saint Michael to save him. In Heaven, the archangel is notified, but refuses to enter the fight without God. The archangel arrives with God over his head and decapitates the dragon, liberating Teodosio from his chains and ending his penance. This legend is associated to the monastery of San Miguel de Aralar. It has been interpreted as a way of justifying the break from the religion and customs of pagan Basques and the adoption of Christianity and, specifically, the veneration for St. Michael. Otherwise, it is very similar to other European legends of knights and dragons, which likely had a significant influence on it.
