description.en: The Sigbin or Sigben is a creature in Philippine mythology said to come out at night to suck the blood of victims from their shadows. It is said to walk backwards with its head lowered between its hind legs, and to have the ability to become invisible to other creatures, especially humans. It resembles a hornless goat, but has very large ears which it can clap like a pair of hands and a long, flexible tail that can be used as a whip. The sigbin is said to emit a nauseating odor. It is believed to issue forth from its lair during Holy Week, looking for children that it will kill for their hearts, which it fashions into amulets. According to the legend, there are families known as Sigbinan ("those who know") whose members possess the power to command these creatures, and are said to keep the sigbin in jars made of clay. The Aswang are said to keep them as pets. There is speculation that the legend may be based on sightings of an actual animal species that is rarely seen; based on the description of the sigbin in popular literature, the animal species might be related to the kangaroo. The myth is popularly known in Visayas Islands and Mindanao especially in rural areas. It is also said that it looks like a dog and owned by rich people who hid those creatures in a jar. Other theories suggest that the sigbin might be a vagrant species of macropodidae living in seclusion that made its way to the Philippines from Australia due to migration way back millions of years ago. It was often described by some as having a red-brownish hue suggesting it might be the red kangaroo, although the diet of the sigbin and the kangaroo are far from similar since the latter is an herbivore. Some theories debunked it as for the fact that the Wallace Line is responsible for separating species that exists within the areas of Sulawesi, Lombok, New Guinea, and Australia from Mainland Southeast Asia, Borneo, Java, Sumatra, Bali, and The Philippines.

description.en: Sihuhata (Thai: แมงสี่หูห้าตา, Maeng Sihuhata, lit. 'four ears, five eyes') is a legendary creature in Lanna folklore of northern Thailand. It is usually described as a large animal with four ears and five eyes. In one Lanna manuscript version, it resembles a bear, eats burning charcoal, and produces gold as excrement. The creature is often associated with Chiang Rai, where it appears in local traditions connected with Wat Phra That Doi Khao Kwai. In some traditions, Sihuhata is identified with the Hindu deity Indra, who takes the creature's form to test a person's virtue.

description.en: The Sin-you (Japanese 神羊, shin'yō, also called Hiai Chai, Chiai Tung, or Kai Tsi) is a mythical creature known throughout various East Asian cultures. The appearance of the Sin-you is similar to that of a Qilin, but more feral and imposing. It is a large quadruped with a feline or ovine body, a shaggy mane, and is either depicted with hooves or feline paws (the latter often to stress its difference from the Qilin). It has a single, unbranching horn in the center of its head, like a western unicorn. The Sin-you’s eyes are said to be very intense and imposing, figuratively burning into whomever it gazes at in a predatory fashion. The Sin-you is highly symbolic of justice, and is believed to have the power to know if a person is lying or know if they are guilty with a glance. It sometimes depicted at court beside the ruler or judge: if a person told a falsehood in its presence, it would leap forward and impale the perjurer though the heart with its horn. In other instances, the judge would put convicted murderers before the Sin-you, who would slay them in the same fashion if they were truly the perpetrator, but leave the innocent unharmed.

description.en: The Sirin (Russian: Сирин) is a legendary creature in Russian folklore, with the head of a beautiful woman and the body of a bird (usually an owl), often equated with sirens in Greek mythology. According to myth, the Sirin lived in Iriy or around the Euphrates River. The Sirin is considered the bird of happiness; it is related to the Alkonost, the bird of sorrow.

description.en: Slag Pile Annie is the name of a ghost reputed to haunt the former Jones and Laughlin Steel Corporation mill in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. According to the story, she appeared as a rough-looking woman wearing a red bandana, working or just standing in a remote and hard-to-access part of the mill. The steelworkers who warned her of danger did not know she was a ghost, until she replied, "I can't get killed, I'm already dead." The tale may have developed from the true experiences of women working dangerous jobs in the Pittsburgh steel mills during World War II.

description.en: The Sluagh (Irish: [ˈsˠl̪ˠuə], Scottish Gaelic: [ˈs̪l̪ˠuəɣ]; Old Irish: slúag; English: 'host, army, crowd'), or Sluagh na marbh ('host of the dead'), were the hosts of the unforgiven dead in Irish and Scottish folklore. In the words of British folklorist Lewis Spence, "In the Western Isles of Scotland the Sluagh, or fairy host, was regarded as composed of the souls of the dead flying through the air, and the feast of the dead at Hallowe'en was likewise the festival of the fairies." Usually taking a crescent form, similar to a flight of birds, they were said to be able to approach and pick up a person from any direction and then transport them far away through the air, from one island to another. Although they would sometimes rescue humans from dangerous rock clefts, they were generally portrayed as dangerous to mortals.

claims.statement_id: Bayangan terbang berputar (ombre volante), jari panjang berselaput, kaki bercakar; bau daging busuk (viande pourrie).
claims.quote: Le Sluagh était décrit comme une ombre volante et tourbillonnante avec de longs doigts maigres et palmés et des jambes déformées qui se terminaient par de longues griffes. Les troupeaux de Sluagh produisaient de l'ombre et un bruit de battements d'ailes et dégageait une odeur de viande pourrie.

claims.statement: The Sluagh attacked the dying (mourants) still weak in their beds.
claims.statement_id: Sluagh menyerang orang sekarat (mourants) yang masih di ranjang dan lemah.
claims.quote: Le Sluagh s'en prenait aux mourants alors qu'ils étaient encore dans leur lit et faibles.

claims.statement: At first the Sluagh could take any form; later it took human appearance (apparence humaine).
claims.statement_id: Mula-mula Sluagh dapat berwujud apa pun, lalu berwujud manusia (apparence humaine).
claims.quote: Au début, le Sluagh pouvait prendre n'importe quelle forme. Il a pris une apparence humaine dans un deuxième temps.

description.en: In the folklore of Northumbria, the Sockburn Worm was a ferocious wyvern that laid waste to the village of Sockburn in Durham. It was said that the beast was finally slain by John Conyers. The tale is said to be the inspiration for Lewis Carroll's poem Jabberwocky which he wrote while in Croft-on-Tees and Whitburn.

claims.statement: Sockburn Worm is documented as folklore northumbria sockburn in regional lore.
claims.statement_id: Sockburn Worm adalah figur mitologis dalam catatan cerita rakyat.
claims.quote: In the folklore of Northumbria, the Sockburn Worm was a ferocious wyvern that laid waste to the village of Sockburn in Durham.

description.id: Soucouyant atau Loogaroo adalah makhluk dalam mitologi Karibia yang mirip dengan vampir. Loogaroo adalah perempuan tua yang bersekutu dengan iblis. Dia memiliki kekuatan gaib dengan syarat setiap malam harus memberi persembahan darah pada iblis. Jika syarat itu tidak terpenuhi maka sang iblis akan mengambil darah dari perempuan itu sampai mati. Loogaroo bisa menanggalkan kulitnya (biasanya dilakukan di bawah "Pohon Iblis", yaitu pohon kapas sutra) dan berubah menjadi nyala api atau bola cahaya biru lalu bergentayangan sepanjang malam untuk mencari darah untuk persembahannya. Setelah mengumpulkan cukup banyak darah, dia akan kembali memakai kulitnya dan berubah menjadi manusia. Jika melihat biji-bijian yang tercecer, Longaroo akan berhenti dan menghitung semuanya, oleh karena itu gundukan pasir atau biji sering disimpan di depan pintu untuk berjaga-jaga dari serangan Longaroo, setidaknya sampai pagi hari. Dalam beberapa cerita, kulit longaroo yang disimpan di Pohon Iblis juga bisa diambil oleh orang lain supaya Longaroo tak bisa menemukan kulitnya.
description.en: A soucouyant, among other names, is a kind of shape-shifting, blood-sucking hag present in Caribbean folklore.

claims.statement: A soucouyant is a kind of shape-shifting, blood-sucking hag of Caribbean folklore.
claims.statement_id: Soucouyant adalah sejenis nenek sihir pengubah wujud dan pengisap darah dalam cerita rakyat Karibia.
claims.quote: is a kind of shape-shifting, blood-sucking hag present in Caribbean folklore.

claims.statement: In Guyana, Belize and Jamaica it is called Ol' Higue or Ole Haig.
claims.statement_id: Di Guyana, Belize, dan Jamaika ia disebut Ol' Higue atau Ole Haig.
claims.quote: Ol' Higue or Ole Haig in Guyana, Belize and Jamaica

claims.statement: By day the Soucouyant looks like a reclusive old woman (or man); at night it strips off its wrinkled skin, puts it in a mortar and flies as a fireball in search of a victim.
claims.statement_id: Pada siang hari Soucouyant tampak sebagai perempuan (atau lelaki) tua penyendiri; pada malam hari ia melepas kulit keriputnya, menaruhnya di lesung, lalu terbang sebagai bola api mencari korban.
claims.quote: The Soucouyant is a folklore character who appears as a reclusive old woman (or man) by day. By night, they strip off their wrinkled skin and put it in a mortar. In the form of a fireball, they fly across the dark sky in search of a victim.

claims.statement: Soucouyants suck blood from the arms, necks and legs of sleeping victims, leaving black and blue marks by morning.
claims.statement_id: Soucouyant mengisap darah dari lengan, leher, dan kaki korban yang tidur, meninggalkan memar biru kehitaman pada pagi harinya.
claims.quote: Soucouyants suck humans' blood from their arms, necks, legs and other soft regions while the victim sleeps, leaving black and blue marks on the body in the morning.

claims.statement: They trade their victims' blood for evil powers with Bazil, the demon living in the silk cotton tree.
claims.statement_id: Mereka menukar darah korban dengan kekuatan jahat dari Bazil, iblis yang tinggal di pohon kapuk.
claims.quote: Soucouyants trade their victims' blood for evil powers with Bazil, the demon who resides in the silk cotton tree.

claims.statement: To expose a soucouyant, people heap rice around the house or at the village crossroads; it must gather the rice grain by grain and is caught in the act.
claims.statement_id: Untuk membongkar soucouyant, orang menaburkan beras di sekitar rumah atau di persimpangan desa; makhluk itu terpaksa memungutinya butir demi butir hingga tertangkap basah.
claims.quote: To expose a soucouyant, it is believed one should heap rice around their house or at the village crossroads; the creature will be obligated to gather the rice, grain by grain, and be caught in the act.

claims.statement: In Trinidad and Tobago the soucouyant is a mythological blood-sucking being.
claims.statement_id: Di Trinidad dan Tobago, soucouyant adalah makhluk mitologis pengisap darah.
claims.quote: Eine Soucouyant ist in Trinidad und Tobago ein mythologisches, blutsaugendes Wesen.

claims.statement: A Christian cross in the window is believed to protect a house from the soucouyant.
claims.statement_id: Salib Kristen di jendela rumah dipercaya melindungi dari pengaruh soucouyant.
claims.quote: Steht am Fenster des Hauses ein christliches Kreuz, so soll dies vor dem Einfluss der Soucouyant schützen.

description.en: The spirit turtle (Chinese: 靈龜) or spirit tortoise is a turtle originated from Chinese mythology and spread with East Asian cultural sphere. It is believed by East Asian cultures, like other turtles in mythology, to represent longevity (壽命). It is said to be chief among all shelled creatures.

claims.quote: The spirit turtle (Chinese: 靈龜) or spirit tortoise is a turtle originated from Chinese mythology and spread with East Asian cultural sphere.

description.en: The stoor worm, or Mester Stoor Worm, was a gigantic evil sea serpent of Orcadian folklore, capable of contaminating plants and destroying animals and humans with its putrid breath. It is probably an Orkney variant of the Norse Jörmungandr, also known as the Midgard Serpent, or world serpent, and has been described as a sea dragon. The king of one country threatened by the beast's arrival was advised to offer it a weekly sacrifice of seven virgins. In desperation, the king eventually issued a proclamation offering his kingdom, his daughter's hand in marriage, and a magic sword to anyone who could destroy the monster. Assipattle, the youngest son of a local farmer, defeated the creature; as it died its teeth fell out to become the islands of Orkney, Shetland and the Faroes, and its body became Iceland. Similarities between Assipatle's defeat of the monster and other dragon-slayer tales, including Herakles' destruction of a sea monster to save Hesione, have been noted by several authors. It has been suggested that tales of this genre evolved during a period of enlightenment when human sacrifices to bestial divinities were beginning to be suppressed.

description.id: Strix adalah burung pembawa pertanda buruk dalam legenda Romawi kuno. Strix digambarkan memakan daging dan darah, seperti vampir. Namun Strix bukanlah roh jahat atau mayat hidup melainkan hasil dari perubahan wujud. Namanya berasal dari Yunani kuno. Strix sering digambarkan sebagai burung hantu.
description.en: The strix (plural striges or strixes), in the mythology of classical antiquity, was a bird of ill omen, the product of metamorphosis, that fed on human flesh and blood. It also referred to witches and related malevolent folkloric beings.

claims.statement: In classical mythology the strix was an ill-omened bird, product of metamorphosis, that fed on human flesh and blood.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Klasik, strix adalah burung pembawa sial hasil perubahan wujud yang memakan daging dan darah manusia.
claims.quote: in the mythology of classical antiquity, was a bird of ill omen, the product of metamorphosis, that fed on human flesh and blood.

claims.statement: The term also referred to witches and similar malevolent beings.
claims.statement_id: Istilah ini juga dipakai untuk penyihir dan makhluk jahat serupa.
claims.quote: It also referred to witches and related malevolent folkloric beings.

claims.statement: In Ovid's Fasti the strix is a large-headed bird with staring eyes, a rapacious beak, greyish-white wings and hooked claws.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fasti karya Ovidius, strix digambarkan berkepala besar, bermata menatap tajam, berparuh pemangsa, bersayap putih keabuan, dan bercakar bengkok.
claims.quote: The strix is described as a large-headed bird with transfixed eyes, rapacious beak, greyish white wings, and hooked claws in Ovid's Fasti.

description.id: Succubus (jamak:: succubi) adalah setan wanita atau entitas supranatural dalam cerita rakyat yang muncul dalam mimpi untuk merayu pria, sebagian besar melalui aktivitas seksual. Menurut beberapa cerita rakyat, succubus membutuhkan air mani untuk bertahan hidup; aktivitas seksual yang berulang-ulang dengan succubus akan menghasilkan ikatan antara succubus dan orang tersebut; dan succubus akan menguras atau menyakiti pria yang berhubungan dengannya. Dalam representasi modern, succubus sering digambarkan sebagai penggoda cantik atau enchantress, bukan sebagai setan atau menakutkan untuk menarik perhatian orang dan bukannya menakut-nakuti. Pasangan pria untuk succubus adalah incubus. Sasaran dari target incubus dan succubus adalah orang yang tidak kuat iman, tidak bisa menahan syahwat, orang yang tidak setia kepada pasangannya, atau orang yang kesepian. Incubus dan succubus menggunakan wujud wanita cantik atau pria tampan untuk menggoda manusia. Dikatakan bahwa succubus dan incubus tidak bisa berkembang biak. Kalaupun berkembang biak, maka cara berkembang biaknya dikatakan agak aneh. Karena itulah mereka menggunakan media manusia sebagai sarana perkembangbiakan. Dikatakan bahwa cara mereka berkembang biak adalah: Succubus harus merayu dan menyetubuhi manusia berjenis kelamin laki-laki, kemudian sampel sperma dari manusia itu diberikan kepada incubus. Lalu, incubus yang sudah mendapatkan sampel sperma manusia itu menggunakan sperma itu untuk menyetubuhi manusia berjenis kelamin wanita, sehingga manusia itu hamil dan melahirkan bayi. Bayi hasil perkawinan manusia dengan succubus/incubus disebut sebagai cambion. Cambion dikatakan akan tumbuh seperti anak-anak normal di usia sebelum 7 tahun, kemudian ketika usianya menginjak 7 tahun, cambion mulai menunjukkan perilaku jahat dan biadabnya, dan akan menjadi generasi penerus incubus dan succubus.
description.en: A succubus (pl. succubi) is a female demon who was described in various European folklore as appearing in the dreams of male humans in order to seduce them. Repeated interactions between a succubus and a man will lead to sexual activity. The establishment and perpetuation of such a relationship enables the production of a hybrid child known as a cambion, but at the expense of the man, whose mental and physical health will deteriorate rapidly, eventually resulting in his death if the succubus continues courting him for a protracted period. In modern representations, a succubus is often depicted as a beautiful woman seductress or charming, rather than as demonic or frightening, to attract people instead of repulsing them. The male counterpart of the succubus is the incubus. Historically, folkloric belief in succubi was motivated by distressing nighttime phenomena, chiefly wet dreams and sleep paralysis. In medieval Europe, union of an incubus or succubus and a human was supposed by some to result in the birth of beings half-demon and half-human children. Legendary magician Merlin was said to have been fathered by an incubus.

claims.quote: The term derives from Late Latin succuba "paramour" from succubare "to lie beneath" (sub- "under" and cubare "to lie"), used to describe this being's implied sexual position relative to the sleeper's position. The English word "succubus" dates from the late 14th century.

claims.quote: A succubus may take the form of a beautiful woman, but closer inspection may reveal deformities of her body, such as bird-like claws or serpentine tails.

claims.statement: According to the Malleus Maleficarum by Heinrich Kramer (1486), succubi collect semen from the men they seduce, and incubi then use it to impregnate women, explaining how demons could seemingly father children.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Malleus Maleficarum karya Heinrich Kramer (1486), succubi mengumpulkan air mani dari lelaki yang dirayunya, lalu incubi memakainya untuk menghamili perempuan, yang menjelaskan bagaimana iblis seolah dapat beranak.

claims.statement: Children so begotten, cambions, were thought to be born deformed or more open to supernatural influence.
claims.statement_id: Anak-anak hasilnya, cambion, dianggap lahir cacat atau lebih rentan terhadap pengaruh gaib.
claims.quote: Children so begotten—cambions—were supposed to be those that were born deformed, or more susceptible to supernatural influences.

claims.quote: 男性形のインキュバスとは表裏一体で、サキュバスの姿で男性から精液を採取し、それをインキュバスに変身後に女性へと注いで望まぬ妊娠をさせる存在とトマス・アクィナスは『神学大全』で記述しており、両性具有の同一者であるとも言われている。

description.en: Other than the many gods and goddesses of the Slavs, the ancient Slavs believed in and revered many supernatural beings that existed in nature. These supernatural beings in Slavic religion come in various forms, and the same name of any single being can be spelled or transliterated differently according to language and transliteration system.

claims.statement: Besides the many Slavic gods and goddesses, the ancient Slavs believed in and revered many supernatural beings of nature, in various forms, whose names can be spelled differently by language and transliteration.
claims.statement_id: Selain banyak dewa dan dewi, bangsa Slavia kuno percaya dan menghormati banyak makhluk gaib di alam, yang beragam wujudnya, dan nama satu makhluk dapat dieja berbeda menurut bahasa dan sistem transliterasi.

These supernatural beings in Slavic religion come in various forms, and the same name of any single being can be spelled or transliterated differently according to language and transliteration system.

claims.statement: The vila is a nymph-like fairy, identified as a nymph by the Greek historian Procopius; the name shares its root with Veles.
claims.statement_id: Vila adalah peri mirip nimfa yang oleh sejarawan Yunani Procopius disebut nimfa; namanya berakar sama dengan nama Veles.
claims.quote: is a fairy that is similar to a nymph, identified as a nymph by the Greek historian Procopius; their name comes from the same root as the name of Veles.

claims.statement: Vile are described as beautiful, eternally young, dressed in white, with thunder-flashing eyes, wings and blonde hair.
claims.statement_id: Vila digambarkan cantik, muda selamanya, berbaju putih, bermata berkilat seperti guntur, bersayap, dan berambut pirang. Bagi Slavia Selatan dan sebagian Slovakia, vila adalah makhluk perempuan yang umumnya bersifat baik.
claims.quote: They are described as beautiful, eternally young, dressed in white, with eyes flashing like thunder, and provided with wings, and blonde hair.

claims.statement: In the beliefs and folklore of the South Slavs and partly the Slovaks, the vila is a female mythological being with mainly positive qualities.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan dan cerita rakyat Slavia Selatan dan sebagian Slovakia, vila adalah makhluk mitologis perempuan yang umumnya bersifat baik.
claims.quote: в верованиях и фольклоре южных славян и отчасти словаков женское мифологическое существо, наделяемое преимущественно положительными свойствами.

description.en: In Turkic mythology, a Susulu (Susuna or Susona) is a legendary aquatic creature with the upper body of a female human and the tail of a fish. Also known as Suna or Sona, she is the daughter of the Sea King.

claims.statement: In Turkic mythology, a Susulu is a legendary aquatic creature with the upper body of a female human and the tail of a fish.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Turkik, Susulu adalah makhluk air legendaris dengan tubuh bagian atas wanita dan ekor ikan.
claims.quote: In Turkic mythology, a Susulu (Susuna or Susona) is a legendary aquatic creature with the upper body of a female human and the tail of a fish.

claims.statement: Also known as Suna or Sona, she is the daughter of the Sea King.
claims.statement_id: Dikenal juga sebagai Suna atau Sona, ia adalah putri dari Raja Laut.
claims.quote: Also known as Suna or Sona, she is the daughter of the Sea King.

claims.statement: Susulus appear in Turkic folklore as unlucky omens, foretelling and provoking disaster.
claims.statement_id: Susulu muncul dalam cerita rakyat Turkik sebagai pertanda buruk pembawa bencana.
claims.quote: Susulus appear in Turkic folklore as unlucky omens, both foretelling disaster and provoking it like mermaids.

claims.statement: They are conventionally depicted as beautiful creatures with long flowing hair.
claims.statement_id: Mereka biasanya digambarkan sebagai makhluk berparas jelita dengan rambut panjang terurai.

claims.statement: Susulus have also been described as able to swim up rivers to freshwater lakes.

description.en: A sylph (also called sylphid) is an air spirit stemming from the 16th-century works of Paracelsus, who describes sylphs as (invisible) beings of the air, his elementals of air. A significant number of subsequent literary and occult works have been inspired by Paracelsus's concept: Robert Alfred Vaughan noted that "the wild but poetical fantasies" of Paracelsus had probably exercised a larger influence over his age and the subsequent one than is generally supposed, particularly on the Rosicrucians, but that through the 18th century they had become reduced to "machinery for the playwright" and "opera figurantes with wings of gauze and spangles".

claims.statement: A sylph is an air spirit from the 16th-century works of Paracelsus, who describes sylphs as invisible beings of the air.
claims.statement_id: Sylph atau sylphid adalah roh udara yang berasal dari karya abad ke-16 oleh Paracelsus yang menggambarkannya sebagai makhluk udara yang tidak terlihat.
claims.quote: A sylph (also called sylphid) is an air spirit stemming from the 16th-century works of Paracelsus, who describes sylphs as (invisible) beings of the air, his elementals of air.

claims.statement: The Swiss-German physician and alchemist Paracelsus coined the term sylph in the 16th century to describe an air spirit among four Classical elements.
claims.statement_id: Alkemis Swiss-German Paracelsus menciptakan istilah sylph pada abad ke-16 untuk menggambarkan roh udara dalam skema empat elemen klasik.
claims.quote: The Swiss–German physician and alchemist Theophrastus von Hohenheim ("Paracelsus") first coined the term sylph in the 16th century to describe an air spirit in his overarching scheme of elemental spirits associated with the four Classical elements.

claims.statement: Sylph is possibly a blend of Latin sylvestris and nympha.

claims.quote: "Sylph" is possibly a blend of from Latin sylvestris and nympha, sylvestris being a common synonym for sylph in Paracelsus.

claims.statement_id: Silvestris dipandang sebagai bentuk pendek dari nympha silvestris yang berarti nimfa hutan.
claims.quote: Anthony Trollope notes a similar usage in the Aeneid, where silvestris is taken as an elliptical form of nympha silvestris ("forest nymph").

claims.quote: Bis in die erste Hälfte des 20. Jahrhunderts bezeichnete man auch ein zartes und anmutiges Mädchen als Sylphide (nach dem Ballett La Sylphide).

description.en: Tahoe Tessie is a cryptid said to inhabit the depths of Lake Tahoe, a lake that straddles the border between California and Nevada. Reports of Tessie date back to the mid-19th century, and over time, the creature has become a well-known part of local folklore.

claims.statement: Tahoe Tessie is a cryptid said to inhabit the depths of Lake Tahoe, on the border of California and Nevada.
claims.statement_id: Tahoe Tessie adalah kriptid yang konon menghuni kedalaman Lake Tahoe, danau di perbatasan California dan Nevada.
claims.quote: Tahoe Tessie is a cryptid said to inhabit the depths of Lake Tahoe, a lake that straddles the border between California and Nevada.

claims.statement: Reports of Tessie date back to the mid-19th century, and it has become a well-known part of local folklore.

claims.quote: Reports of Tessie date back to the mid-19th century, and over time, the creature has become a well-known part of local folklore.

claims.statement: One of the earliest accounts dates from 1865, when I.C. Coggin of San Francisco reported a massive serpent-like creature.

claims.quote: One of the earliest accounts of a large creature in Lake Tahoe comes from 1865, when I.C. Coggin, a socialite from San Francisco, reported seeing a massive serpent-like creature.

claims.statement: One prominent theory holds that the creature could be a giant sturgeon.

claims.quote: One prominent theory suggests that the creature could be a giant sturgeon, a prehistoric-looking fish known to grow to large sizes.

claims.quote: According to limnologist Charles Goldman of the UC Davis Tahoe Research Group, many sightings of Tessie, particularly those describing humps or waves, could be caused by wind patterns or water movements

claims.statement: By the late 20th century, Tessie had become a lighthearted local figure, often depicted as a friendly dragon.
claims.statement_id: Menjelang akhir abad ke-20, Tessie menjadi tokoh yang lebih ceria dalam budaya setempat dan sering digambarkan sebagai naga yang ramah.
claims.quote: By the late 20th century, Tessie had become a more lighthearted figure in local culture, often depicted as a friendly dragon.

description.en: The talamaur is a vampire legend of the Banks Islands, Vanuatu, located in the South Pacific. A talamaur was a type of vampire who controlled the ghost of a dead person, and could use it to drain the vitality from the living and the recently deceased. Some people actually aspired to become talamaurs. The power of a talamaur could purportedly be gained by eating part of a corpse, thus gaining kinship with the soul of the deceased. A talamaur could be identified by exposure to the smoke of certain burning leaves, which would cause it to shout the names of the deceased person whose ghost it controlled and of the person whom it was afflicting. Injuries inflicted on the talamaur's ghostly form would appear on its living body; such bruising was used to identify a talamaur.

description.en: Taotao Mo'na, also commonly written as taotaomona or taotaomo'na (Chamoru taotao, "person/people" and mo'na "precede", loosely translated as "people before history" or "ancient people"), are spirits of ancient giant inhabitants believed to protect the mountains and wild places of the Mariana Islands, which include Luta, Saipan, Tinian and Guam, in Micronesia. Belief in Taotao Mo'na is present throughout these islands.

description.en: A tarand, also known as a tarandos, tarandus, parandrus, or parandros, is a legendary reindeer/moose-like creature with chameleon properties. It was first described in Aristotle's Corpus Aristotelicum as Tarandos (Τάρανδος). It was also mentioned in Pliny's History of the Animals (Tarandus), Aelian's De Natura Animalium (Tarandos), Solinus (Parandrus) and Caesar, appearing again in key texts of the medieval period, such as The York Mystery Cycle (1440) and Francois Rabelais' Pantagruel (1552). The veracity of the tarand was discussed by Jean Léopold Nicolas Frédéric, Baron Cuvier (1769–1832). Aristotle, Pliny and Aelian write that the animal (Tarandus) was living in Scythia, while Solinus write that the animal that he describes (Parandus) was living in Aethiopia.

description.en: Teju Jagua is the first son of Tau and Kerana and one of the seven legendary monsters of Guaraní mythology. Because of the curse placed upon Tau by Arasy for raping Kerana, Tau's descendants were forever cursed to a deformed and monstrous appearance. Thus, the pair's first son was a huge lizard with seven dog-heads and eyes that shoot out fire. His seven dog-heads make any movement difficult. Some versions of the story say Teju Jagua has only one giant dog-head. But all versions agree that he has a limited ability to move around. His appearance was the most horrid of all the seven brothers. However, his ferocity was tempered by choice of Tupã. He was left calm and harmless. Still he was feared for his fiery gaze. He feeds on fruit and his brother Yasy Yateré gave him honey, his favorite food. He is considered the lord of the caves and protector of fruit. He is also mentioned as a brilliant protector of buried treasure. Its skin became shiny after rolling around in the gold and precious stones of Itapé.

description.en: The Black Dog of Newgate is a legend concerning the haunting of the former Newgate Prison of London, which was located next to the Old Bailey (The Central Criminal Court), close to St. Paul's Cathedral, in London, England. This account of a haunting based at the prison is an example of the English Black Dog category of supernatural manifestations, featuring a spectral hound of ill-omen or malicious intent, which is a notable archetype in British folklore and superstition. The earliest account of the story dates from the publication The Discovery of a London Monster, called The Blacke Dogg of Newgate: Profitable for all Readers to Take Heed by.

description.id: Kaki Berbulu (Portugis:perna cabeluda) adalah sebuah legenda urban dari Brasil yang berasal dari kota Recife. Legenda ini pertama kali muncul melalui surat kabar Diario de Pernambuco pada masa kediktatoran militer di Brasil tahun 1970-an. Surat kabar tersebut menggunakan narasi fiksi tentang Kaki Berbulu untuk menggantikan dan menandai materi yang terkena sensor. Makhluk ini digambarkan sebagai sebuah kaki manusia berbulu yang menyerang orang dengan cara menubruk dan menendang pada malam hari. Setelah laporan pertama di Diario de Pernambuco, Kaki Berbulu dengan cepat menjadi bagian dari imajinasi populer masyarakat Recife. Program radio, karya sastra, serta lagu dan arak-arakan karnaval menampilkan Kaki Berbulu, meskipun laporan tentang makhluk ini sempat menimbulkan ketakutan publik di Recife pada tahun-tahun awal kemunculannya. Dalam beberapa dekade berikutnya, Kaki Berbulu kembali diadaptasi dalam musik, komik, dan bioskop. Film The Secret Agent (2025) menjadikannya sebagai elemen utama dalam narasinya.
description.en: The Hairy Leg (Portuguese: perna cabeluda) is a Brazilian urban legend that originated in the city of Recife. It was conceived by the newspaper Diário de Pernambuco during the Brazilian military dictatorship in the 1970s. The newspaper used fictional narratives about the Leg to replace and signal material that had been censored by the regime. The creature is described as a hairy human leg that attacks people at night by tackling and kicking them. After its first reports in Diário de Pernambuco, the Hairy Leg quickly became established in Recife's popular imagination. Radio programmes, literature, carnival songs and floats all featured the Hairy Leg, although reports of the creature generated public fear in Recife during the first years of its appearance. Over the decades the Hairy Leg has been reappropriated in music, comics, and cinema. The film The Secret Agent (2025) (Portuguese: O Agente Secreto) incorporated it as a central element of its narrative.

description.en: Thinan-malkia is an evil spirit in Australian Aboriginal mythology that captures victims with nets that entangle their feet.

description.en: Tianlong (simplified Chinese: 天龙; traditional Chinese: 天龍; pinyin: tiānlóng; Wade–Giles: t'ien lung; lit. "heavenly dragon") is a flying dragon in Chinese mythology, a star in Chinese astrology, and a proper name.

claims.statement: Tianlong is a flying dragon in Chinese mythology, with the same name also used astronomically.
claims.statement_id: Tianlong adalah naga terbang dalam mitologi Tiongkok; nama yang sama juga memiliki penggunaan astronomis.
claims.quote: Tianlong (simplified Chinese: 天龙; traditional Chinese: 天龍; pinyin: tiānlóng; Wade–Giles: t'ien lung; lit. "heavenly dragon") is a flying dragon in Chinese mythology, a star in Chinese astrology, and a proper name.

claims.statement: Its name combines elements for heaven and dragon.
claims.statement_id: Namanya menggabungkan unsur langit dan naga.
claims.quote: The term tianlong combines tian 天 "heaven" and long 龍 "dragon". Since tian literally means "heaven; the heavens; sky" or figuratively "Heaven; God; gods", tianlong can denote "heavenly dragon; celestial dragon" or "holy dragon; divine dragon".

claims.statement: The dragon Tianlong differs from the homonymous Heavenly Deaf attendant of Wenchang Wang.
claims.statement_id: Tianlong sang naga dibedakan dari Tianlong bermakna tuli surgawi, pengiring Wenchang Wang.
claims.quote: Tianlong 天龍 is homophonous with another name in Chinese folklore. Tianlong 天聾 "Heavenly Deaf" (with the character long 聾 "deaf" combining the "ear radical" 耳 and a long 龍 phonetic element) and Diya 地啞 "Earthly Dumb" are legendary attendants to Wenchang Wang 文昌王, the patron deity of literature.

claims.statement: Its Buddhist senses developed to include heavenly nagas or devas and nagas.
claims.statement_id: Maknanya berkembang dalam Buddhisme menjadi naga surgawi atau kelompok dewa dan naga.
claims.quote: From originally denoting "heavenly dragon", Tianlong 天龍 semantically developed meanings as Buddhist "heavenly Nāgas" or "Devas and Nāgas", "centipede", and "proper names" of stars, people, and places.

claims.statement: The word tianlong is recorded from the Han period.
claims.statement_id: Kata tianlong tercatat sejak zaman Han.
claims.quote: Among Chinese classic texts, tian "heaven" and long "dragon" were first used together in Zhou dynasty (1122 BCE – 256 BCE) writings, but the word tianlong was not recorded until the Han dynasty (207 BCE – 220 CE).

description.en: The Tikbalang (/ˈtikbaˌlaŋ/) (also Tigbalang, Tigbalan, Tikbalan, Tigbolan, or Werehorse) is a creature of Philippine folklore said to lurk in the mountains and rainforests of the Philippines. It is a tall, bony humanoid creature with the head and hooves of a horse and disproportionately long limbs, to the point that its knees reach above its head when it squats down. In some versions, it is a transformation of an aborted fetus sent to earth from limbo.

claims.statement: The tikbalang (also Tigbalang, Tigbalan, Tikbalan, Tigbolan) is a Philippine folklore creature lurking in mountains and rainforests; tall, bony, with a horse's head and hooves and limbs so long its knees pass its head when squatting; in some versions it is an aborted fetus sent from limbo.
claims.statement_id: Tikbalang (juga Tigbalang, Tigbalan, Tikbalan, Tigbolan) adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Filipina yang mengintai di pegunungan dan hutan hujan; tinggi, kurus, berkepala dan berkuku kuda, bertungkai sangat panjang hingga lututnya melewati kepala saat berjongkok; dalam beberapa versi ia jelmaan janin yang digugurkan dan dikirim dari limbo.
claims.quote: is a creature of Philippine folklore said to lurk in the mountains and rainforests of the Philippines. It is a tall, bony humanoid creature with the head and hooves of a horse and disproportionately long limbs, to the point that its knees reach above its head when it squats down. In some versions, it is a transformation of an aborted fetus sent to earth from limbo.

claims.statement: As horses were not native to the pre-Spanish Philippines, the earliest records of the tikbalang do not specify a horse form.
claims.statement_id: Karena kuda bukan hewan asli Filipina sebelum masa Spanyol, catatan tertulis awal tentang tikbalang tidak menyebut wujud kuda.
claims.quote: As horses weren't native to the Philippines in the pre-Spanish era, the earliest written records about the tikbalang did not specify horse or animal morphology.

claims.statement: Plasencia wrote that there were ghosts called vibit and phantoms called Tigbalaang.
claims.statement_id: Plasencia menulis bahwa ada hantu yang disebut vibit dan penampakan yang disebut Tigbalaang.
claims.quote: There were also ghosts, which they called vibit; and phantoms, which they called Tigbalaang.

claims.statement: Among early Tagalogs, the insult 'Tigbalang ca mandin!' ('You are a wild beast!') described someone whose behaviour was improper.
claims.statement_id: Di kalangan orang Tagalog awal, ungkapan hinaan 'Tigbalang ca mandin!' ('Kau binatang liar!') dipakai untuk orang yang berperilaku tidak pantas.
claims.quote: Among the early Tagalogs, the derogatory expression “Tigbalang ca mandin!”, literally translated as “You are a wild beast!”, was used to describe a person whose behavior was considered improper or socially unacceptable.

claims.statement: Juan Francisco de San Antonio's Cronicas (1738-1744) describes the tikbalang as a malevolent mountain being able to take many forms, including horses.
claims.statement_id: Cronicas (1738-1744) karya Juan Francisco de San Antonio menggambarkan tikbalang sebagai makhluk jahat di pegunungan yang dapat berubah menjadi berbagai wujud, termasuk kuda.
claims.quote: Juan Francisco de San Antonio's Cronicas(1738-1744) describes the tikbalang as a malevolent entity living in the mountains, able to shapeshift into a variety of forms, including horses.

claims.statement: According to the Cronicas, it appeared in the mountains as an old man claiming to be their ancestor, as a horse, or as a monster.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Cronicas, tikbalang biasa menampakkan diri di pegunungan sebagai orang tua yang mengaku leluhur mereka, sebagai kuda, atau sebagai monster.
claims.quote: it has been wont to appear to them in the mountains—now in the guise of an old man, telling them that he is their nono; now as a horse; and now as a monster.

claims.statement: The first document describing the tikbalang as a werehorse is Juan José Delgado's Biblioteca Histórica Filipina (c. 1750).
claims.statement_id: Dokumen pertama yang menggambarkan tikbalang sebagai manusia-kuda adalah Biblioteca Histórica Filipina karya Juan José Delgado (sekitar 1750).
claims.quote: However, the very first document to actually describe the tikbalang as specifically having the appearance of a werehorse as it is more commonly known is Juan José Delgado's Biblioteca Histórica Filipina (orig. c. 1750).

claims.statement: Delgado notes the Visayans used the name unglo for the same creature.
claims.statement_id: Delgado menyebut orang Visayas memakai nama unglo untuk makhluk yang sama.
claims.quote: Delgado also mentions the name "unglo" being used by the Visayans to refer to the same creature as the tikbalang.

claims.statement: The tikbalang is linked with dark, lonely, overgrown places such as under bridges, bamboo clumps, banana groves, or atop kalumpang and balete trees.
claims.statement_id: Tikbalang dikaitkan dengan tempat gelap, sepi, dan rimbun, seperti di bawah jembatan, rumpun bambu, kebun pisang, atau di atas pohon kalumpang dan balete.
claims.quote: Tikbalang is generally associated with dark, sparsely populated, foliage-overgrown areas, with legends variously identifying their habitat as being beneath bridges, in bamboo clumps or banana groves, and atop Kalumpang (Sterculia foetida) or Balite (Ficus indica) trees.

claims.statement: Tikbalangs scare and mislead travellers, making them return to the same path; wearing a shirt inside out or asking permission aloud is believed to counter this.
claims.statement_id: Tikbalang menakuti dan menyesatkan pejalan, membuat mereka kembali ke jalan yang sama; memakai baju terbalik atau meminta izin lewat dengan keras dipercaya menangkalnya.
claims.quote: Tikbalangs or Tigbolan scare travelers, lead them astray and play tricks on them such as making them return to an arbitrary path no matter how far they go or turn. Wearing one’s shirt inside out is believed to counteract this. Another countermeasure is to ask permission aloud to pass by

claims.statement: Four colonial records show a progression: an undescribed Tigbalaang (1589), a winged, odorous mountain apparition (1613), a multi-form being (c. 1731), and a giant with horse legs (1763).
claims.statement_id: Empat catatan kolonial menunjukkan perkembangan: Tigbalaang tanpa gambaran fisik (1589), penampakan gunung bersayap dan berbau (1613), makhluk yang dapat berganti wujud (sekitar 1731), dan raksasa berkaki kuda (1763).
claims.quote: Taken together, the four records show an identifiable progression: the named but physically undescribed Tigbalaang in 1589; a winged and odorous mountain apparition in 1613; a being able to assume several forms by about 1731; and a giant with horse legs in 1763.

claims.statement: Some Filipinos still believe tikbalangs inhabit trees as guardians.

claims.quote: San Buenaventura records a belief that the tigbalang had wings and carried people where it wished. Those taken away were said to grow weak and die.

description.en: The tiyanak (also tianak or tianac Tagalog: [ˈtjanak]) is a vampiric creature in Philippine mythology that takes on the form of a toddler or baby. Although there are various types, it typically takes the form of a newborn baby and cries in the jungle to attract unwary travelers. Once it is picked up by an unfortunate passerby, it reverts to its true form and attacks the victim. The tiyanak is also depicted to take malevolent delight in leading travelers astray, or in abducting children.

claims.statement: The tiyanak (also tianak) is a vampiric creature of Philippine mythology in the form of a toddler or baby, usually a crying newborn in the jungle luring travellers; once picked up it reverts and attacks; it also likes to mislead travellers or abduct children.
claims.statement_id: Tiyanak (juga tianak) adalah makhluk pengisap darah dalam mitologi Filipina yang berwujud balita atau bayi, biasanya bayi baru lahir yang menangis di hutan untuk memikat pejalan; begitu diangkat ia kembali ke wujud asli dan menyerang; ia juga senang menyesatkan pejalan atau menculik anak.

Although there are various types, it typically takes the form of a newborn baby and cries in the jungle to attract unwary travelers. Once it is picked up by an unfortunate passerby, it reverts to its true form and attacks the victim.

claims.statement: Plasencia recorded the belief that a woman who died in childbirth was punished with her child and heard lamenting at night; this was called patianac.
claims.statement_id: Plasencia mencatat kepercayaan bahwa perempuan yang mati saat melahirkan dihukum bersama anaknya dan ratapannya terdengar di malam hari; ini disebut patianac.
claims.quote: They had another deception—namely, that if any woman died in childbirth, she and the child suffered punishment; and that, at night, she could be heard lamenting. This was called patianac.

claims.statement: According to Martinez de Zuniga (1803) and San Antonio (1738-44), to counter the patianac the husband stripped naked and brandished a sword until his wife was delivered.
claims.statement_id: Menurut catatan Martinez de Zuniga (1803) dan San Antonio (1738-44), untuk melawan patianac sang suami menanggalkan pakaian dan mengayunkan pedang sampai istrinya selesai bersalin.
claims.quote: To counteract the malignity of this spirit, the husband, fastening the door, reduces himself to a state of complete nudity, lights a fire, and arming himself with his sword, continues to flourish it furiously, until the woman is delivered.

claims.statement: In one version it keeps a baby's shape but grows sharp claws and fangs; in another its true form is a little old man with wrinkled skin and a long beard and moustache.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu versi tiyanak tetap berbentuk bayi tetapi menumbuhkan cakar dan taring tajam; dalam versi lain wujud aslinya kakek kecil berkulit keriput dengan janggut dan kumis panjang.
claims.quote: In one version, it retains the general shape of a baby but then forms sharp claws and fangs to attack its victim.

claims.statement: In the Central Luzon version, especially Pampanga, tiyanak are small nut-brown people floating in the air; in a Mindoro legend it turns into a black bird.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi Luzon Tengah, terutama Pampanga, tiyanak adalah orang kecil berkulit cokelat yang melayang di udara; dalam legenda Mindoro ia berubah menjadi burung hitam.
claims.quote: In another version from Central Luzon, especially in Pampanga, the tiyanak are described as small, nut-brown people who don't walk on the ground but rather float on air.

claims.statement: The Mandaya of Mindanao say the tiyanak is the spirit of a child whose mother died before giving birth; a similar Malay being is the pontianak.
claims.statement_id: Orang Mandaya di Mindanao percaya tiyanak adalah arwah anak yang ibunya meninggal sebelum melahirkan; makhluk serupa dalam cerita rakyat Melayu adalah pontianak.
claims.quote: The Mandaya people of Mindanao claim that the tiyanak is the spirit of a child whose mother died before giving birth.

claims.statement: With 16th-century Spanish colonization, the tiyanak myth merged with Catholicism: tiyanak became souls of infants who died unbaptized, and today also aborted fetuses returning for revenge.
claims.statement_id: Dengan penjajahan Spanyol pada abad ke-16, mitos tiyanak dipadukan dengan Katolik: tiyanak dianggap arwah bayi yang meninggal sebelum dibaptis, dan kini juga janin yang digugurkan yang kembali membalas dendam.
claims.quote: With the Spanish colonization of the Philippines in the 16th century, the tiyanak myth was integrated into Catholicism. The tiyanak in the Catholic version were supposedly the souls of infants that died before being baptized.

claims.statement: Those led astray by its cries can break the spell by turning their clothes inside out; loud noises like New Year celebrations are also believed to drive it away.
claims.statement_id: Orang yang tersesat karena tangisannya dapat mematahkan pesonanya dengan membalik pakaian; suara keras seperti perayaan Tahun Baru juga dipercaya mengusirnya.
claims.quote: Those that were led astray by the creature's cries are believed to be able to break the enchantment by turning their clothes inside out.

claims.statement: The patianac account is from Fr. Juan de Plasencia on the Tagalogs (1589).
claims.statement_id: Catatan tentang patianac berasal dari Fr. Juan de Plasencia tentang orang Tagalog (1589).

description.en: In Nguni mythology, the tokoloshe, tikoloshe, tikolosh, tonkolosh, tonkolosi, tokolotshe, thokolosi, or hili is a dwarf-like water spirit. It is a mischievous and evil spirit that can become invisible by drinking water or swallowing a stone. Tokoloshes are called upon by malevolent people to cause trouble for others. At its least harmful, a tokoloshe can be used to scare children, but its power extends to causing illness or even the death of the victim. Protection against them includes traditional methods such as raising beds off the ground and interventions by spiritual figures like pastors with an apostolic calling or traditional healers (sangomas), who are seen to possess the power to banish them. The tokoloshe is often referenced satirically to critique the influence of superstitions on behaviour and society.

description.id: Toyotama-hime (豊玉姫), lebih dikenal sebagai Otohime (乙姫), adalah seorang dewi dalam mitologi Jepang, dan muncul dalam Kojiki dan Nihon Shoki. Ia adalah putri cantik dari Ryūjin, dewa laut. Ia menikahi sebuah pemburu yang bernama Hoori dan melahirkan seorang putra, yang kemudian menghasilkan Kaisar Jimmu, Kaisar Jepang pertama.
description.en: Toyotama-hime (Japanese: 豊玉姫) is a goddess in Japanese mythology who appears in Kojiki and Nihon Shoki. She is the daughter of the sea deity, Watatsumi, and the wife of Hoori. She is known as the paternal grandmother of Emperor Jimmu, the first emperor of Japan. Toyotama marries the prince Hoori, but returns to the sea when he breaks the vow not to spy on her while she goes through childbirth. The child she gave birth to was Ugayafukiaezu.

claims.statement: Toyotama-hime is Watatsumi’s daughter, Hohodemi’s consort, and Ugayafukiaezu’s mother.
claims.statement_id: Toyotama-hime adalah putri Watatsumi, istri Hohodemi, dan ibu Ugayafukiaezu.
claims.quote: Daughter of the sea kami Watatsumi, Toyotamabime was the consort of Hohodemi and mother of Ugayafukiaezu.

claims.statement: Toyotama-hime met Hohodemi in the undersea palace.
claims.statement_id: Toyotama-hime bertemu Hohodemi di istana bawah laut.
claims.quote: When Hohodemi visited Watatsumi's undersea palace, Toyotamabime met him and, entranced by his appearance, immediately informed her father of his arrival.

claims.statement: Hohodemi returned to land after three years.
claims.statement_id: Setelah tiga tahun, Hohodemi pulang ke daratan.
claims.quote: She thereafter became his wife, but after three years, she became aware of her husband's longing for home, and Hohodemi subsequently returned to the land.

claims.statement: Her marriage and motherhood appear in the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki.
claims.statement_id: Perkawinan dan keibuannya dikisahkan dalam Kojiki dan Nihon Shoki.
claims.quote: Detailed accounts of her marriage and motherhood are provided by both Kojiki and Nihongi.

claims.statement: She requested a birthing hut thatched with cormorant feathers.
claims.statement_id: Ia meminta pondok bersalin beratap bulu burung pecuk.
claims.quote: she requested that he build her a parturition hut thatched with cormorant feathers.

claims.statement: She forbade Hohodemi to watch the birth, but he peeped in.
claims.statement_id: Ia melarang Hohodemi melihatnya saat melahirkan, tetapi suaminya mengintip.
claims.quote: Toyotamabime asked Hohodemi not to look upon her as she gave birth, but the curious Hohodemi peeked in

claims.statement: Shamed at being seen in that form, she returned to the sea.
claims.statement_id: Karena malu terlihat dalam wujud itu, ia kembali ke laut.
claims.quote: Enraged and shamed that she had been seen in this form, Toyotamabime returned to her ocean home

claims.statement: The Kojiki and main Nihon Shoki text differ; the latter says dragon.
claims.statement_id: Kojiki dan teks utama Nihon Shoki berbeda tentang wujudnya; yang terakhir menyebut naga.
claims.quote: in Kojiki, this was her original form, but the main text of Nihongi states that she became a dragon

claims.statement: Visitors pray at her shrine for health and beautiful skin.
claims.statement_id: Orang datang ke kuilnya untuk berdoa bagi kesehatan dan kulit yang indah.
claims.quote: Many people come to this shrine to pray for beautiful skin and good health.

claims.statement: Toyotama-hime marries Hoori in the legend.
claims.statement_id: Toyotama-hime menikah dengan Hoori menurut legenda.
claims.quote: Toyotamahime, the story goes, married Prince Hoori no Mikoto, a mythical ancestor of the Japanese imperial line.

description.en: The Tréo-Fall, also known as danserien-noz, are lutin-like creatures from the folklore of Lower Brittany. Under this first name, they are specific to the island of Ushant, where traditions about them were collected by François-Marie Luzel. The Tréo-Fall are said to gather at the top of cliffs to dance in the moonlight, promising treasures to humans who cross their path. Two tales about "night dancers" were collected in Plouaret in January 1869. These goblins reward humans who join in their dance, and punish those who insult them.

claims.statement: Tréo-Fall (danserien-noz), lutin-like, Lower Brittany folklore; island of Ushant; François-Marie Luzel; Breton.
claims.statement_id: Tréo-Fall (danserien-noz), mirip lutin, folklor Basse-Bretagne (Lower Brittany, Prancis); Pulau Ouessant (Ushant); François-Marie Luzel; Breton.
claims.quote: The Tréo-Fall, also known as danserien-noz, are lutin-like creatures from the folklore of Lower Brittany. Under this first name, they are specific to the island of Ushant, where traditions about them were collected by François-Marie Luzel.

claims.statement: Dance on clifftops by moonlight, promising treasure; Plouaret, January 1869.
claims.statement_id: Menari di puncak tebing di bawah bulan, menjanjikan harta; Plouaret, Januari (January) 1869.
claims.quote: The Tréo-Fall are said to gather at the top of cliffs to dance in the moonlight, promising treasures to humans who cross their path. Two tales about "night dancers" were collected in Plouaret in January 1869.

claims.statement: A knife in the ground touched each round; wish granted; dancers often break kidneys; Paul Sébillot: small size.
claims.statement_id: Pisau di tanah disentuh tiap putaran; permintaan dikabulkan; penari sering ginjal rusak; Paul Sébillot: tubuh kecil.
claims.quote: The only way to escape is to stick a knife in the ground, then graze it at each dance circle. If the dancer succeeds in fulfilling this condition, the Tréo-Fall will grant his or her request, whatever it may be.

claims.statement: François-Marie Luzel and Françoise Morvan: a kind of Korrigan; the knife on Ouessant; night dancer (danseur de nuit); reward and punishment.
claims.statement_id: François-Marie Luzel dan Françoise Morvan: jenis Korrigan; pisau di Ouessant; penari malam (danseur de nuit); hadiah dan hukuman.
claims.quote: François-Marie Luzel and Françoise Morvan see the Tréo-Fall as a particular variety of Korrigans, linked to a local use of the knife on the island of Ouessant.

claims.statement: fr article: Tréo-Fall (danserien-noz), lutin-like, Basse-Bretagne.
claims.statement_id: Artikel fr: Tréo-Fall (danserien-noz), mirip lutin, Basse-Bretagne.
claims.quote: Les Tréo-Fall, également connus sous le nom de danserien-noz, sont des créatures du folklore populaire de la Basse-Bretagne, de type lutin.

description.en: A troll cat is the familiar of a witch in Scandinavian folklore. Troll cats sucked milk from cows and spat it out in the witches' milk pails, and went into homes to lick up cream. Aside from cats, similar creatures include the milk rabbit, milk hare, and ball-shaped troll ball.

claims.statement: In Scandinavian folklore the troll cat is a witch's familiar that sucked cows' milk and spat it into the witch's pails and entered homes to lick cream; similar creatures include the milk rabbit, milk hare and troll ball.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia, kucing troll adalah makhluk peliharaan penyihir yang mengisap susu sapi dan memuntahkannya ke ember susu penyihir serta masuk ke rumah untuk menjilat krim; makhluk serupa antara lain kelinci susu, terwelu susu, dan bola troll.
claims.quote: A troll cat is the familiar of a witch in Scandinavian folklore. Troll cats sucked milk from cows and spat it out in the witches' milk pails, and went into homes to lick up cream. Aside from cats, similar creatures include the milk rabbit, milk hare, and ball-shaped troll ball.

claims.statement: Witches reportedly made them from 'human hair, nails, wood shavings and the like'; the Norwegian names trollnøste and trollnøa show a ball-of-yarn shape, while another kind looked like an ordinary cat, and harming it harmed the witch too.
claims.statement_id: Penyihir konon membuatnya dari "rambut manusia, kuku, serutan kayu, dan semacamnya"; nama Norwegia trollnøste dan trollnøa menunjukkan wujud gulungan benang, sedangkan jenis lain tampak seperti kucing biasa, dan melukainya akan melukai penyihir juga.
claims.quote: Witches reportedly were able to create them from "human hair, nails, wood shavings, and the like" ... The Norwegian names trollnøste and trollnøa indicate their shapes: those troll cats looked like balls of yarn. Another kind of troll cat had the appearance of an ordinary cat; but, unlike the ball-shaped troll cat, harming the cat-shaped troll cat would result in the same harm to the witch.

claims.statement: Shooting a troll cat was thought to make milk spray from the wound; it had to be buried with the witch, or she would leave her grave to fetch it. A related creature is the tilberi, a milk thief and witches' aide in Icelandic folklore.
claims.statement_id: Menembak kucing troll diyakini membuat susu menyembur dari lukanya; kucing itu harus dikubur bersama penyihirnya, atau penyihir akan keluar dari kuburnya untuk mengambilnya. Makhluk terkait adalah tilberi, pencuri susu pembantu penyihir dalam cerita rakyat Islandia.
claims.quote: In addition, it was thought that shooting a troll cat would cause milk to spray from its wound. ... The troll cat would have to be buried with the witch, or the witch would have to leave her grave to retrieve it. ... A related creature is the tilberi, a milk thief and witches' aide in Icelandic folklore.

claims.statement: Belief in troll cats seems linked to observing matter (such as hair) regurgitated by cattle; the slime mould Fuligo septica and spittlebug foam were seen as troll-cat droppings.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan pada kucing troll tampaknya berkaitan dengan pengamatan benda (seperti rambut) yang dimuntahkan sapi; jamur lendir Fuligo septica dan busa serangga ludah dianggap kotoran kucing troll.
claims.quote: The existence of troll cats appears to be related to the observation of matter (such as hair) regurgitated by cattle. The slime mold Fuligo septica and the foam made by spittle bugs were seen as troll cat droppings.

claims.statement: In Swedish folk belief a bjära (also mjölkhare, trollhare, trollkatten and others) was a being a witch used to steal neighbours' cows' milk; it could be a hare (Småland), a cat or bird (Dalarna) or a ball of yarn (Norrland).
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Swedia, bjära (juga mjölkhare, trollhare, trollkatten, dan lain-lain) adalah makhluk yang dipakai penyihir untuk mencuri susu sapi tetangga; ia bisa berwujud terwelu (Småland), kucing atau burung (Dalarna), atau gulungan benang (Norrland).
claims.quote: Una bjära (mjölkhare, trollhare, pukhare, puken, trollkatten, baran, bärarn) era, en las creencias populares suecas, un ser característico que una bruja usaba para robar leche de las vacas de los vecinos. Una bjära podía ser una liebre (Småland), un gato o un pájaro (Dalarna) o un ovillo (Norrland).

claims.statement: The first description of how a bjära is made comes from a witch trial at Söderala, Hälsingland, on 15 January 1597.
claims.statement_id: Deskripsi pertama cara membuat bjära berasal dari pengadilan sihir di Söderala, Hälsingland, pada 15 Januari 1597.
claims.quote: La primera descripción de cómo se fabrica una bjära es de un juicio por brujería en Söderala, Hälsingland, el 15-1-1597.

description.id: Tsuchinoko (ツチノコ atau 槌の子) adalah hewan yang dilaporkan ada di Jepang tetapi belum pernah bisa dibuktikan (kriptid). Bentuknya seperti ular tetapi berperut gendut mirip botol atau pin boling dengan ekor yang kecil mirip ekor tikus. Hewan ini dilaporkan pernah "dilihat" saksi mata di berbagai tempat di Jepang, kecuali di Hokkaido dan Kepulauan Ryukyu. Hingga kini, tsuchinoko belum pernah berhasil ditangkap orang karena saksi mata menjadi takut, atau hewan ini lebih dulu melarikan diri. Nama "Tsuchinoko" berasal dari nama lokal untuk "hewan" ini menurut penduduk daerah Kansai (Kyoto, Mie, Nara, dan Shikoku). Di daerah Kanto, penduduk menyebutnya sebagai bachihebi. Beberapa pemerintah daerah di Jepang menawarkan hadiah uang dalam jumlah besar bagi orang yang berhasil menangkap tsuchinoko. Hadiah uang sebesar 100 juta yen pernah ditawarkan kota Itoigawa, Niigata.
description.en: In Japanese folklore, the tsuchinoko (ツチノコ or 槌の子), literally translating to "child of hammer", is a snake-like cryptid. The name tsuchinoko is prevalent in Western Japan, including Kansai and Shikoku; the creature is known as bachi hebi (バチヘビ) in Northeastern Japan.

claims.statement: Tsuchinoko is a thick-bodied snake-like figure said to appear on paths, fields, and riverbanks.
claims.statement_id: Tsuchinoko digambarkan sebagai makhluk mirip ular bertubuh tebal yang terlihat di jalan gunung, ladang, dan tepian sungai.
claims.quote: Tsuchinoko is a mallet-shaped, thick-bodied serpentine monster said to be sighted in mountain paths, fields, and the thickets of riverbanks.

claims.statement: Accounts describe a thirty to eighty centimeter creature with a bottle-thick body.
claims.statement_id: Gambaran setempat menyebut panjang 30–80 sentimeter dan badan setebal botol.
claims.quote: a creature about thirty to eighty centimeters long, with a head protruding from a body thick as a beer bottle

claims.statement: Reported sightings range from Iwate to Kagoshima.
claims.statement_id: Laporan penampakan disebut tersebar dari Iwate sampai Kagoshima.
claims.quote: the national scale of sightings from Iwate Prefecture in the north to Kagoshima Prefecture in the south

claims.statement: Tsuchinoko has varied local names and is not a uniform national figure.
claims.statement_id: Nama tsuchinoko bervariasi menurut daerah.
claims.quote: The multitude of local names indicates that the Tsuchinoko was not a uniform character nationwide.

claims.statement: Tsuchinoko has not been scientifically confirmed.
claims.statement_id: Keberadaan tsuchinoko belum dikonfirmasi secara ilmiah.
claims.quote: a legendary reptilelike creature the existence of which had never been scientifically confirmed.

claims.statement: Tsuchinoko is described as both a yōkai and a cryptid.
claims.statement_id: Tsuchinoko dibicarakan sebagai yōkai sekaligus hewan misterius.
claims.quote: occupying a unique position of being a yokai while simultaneously being a cryptid.

claims.statement: Search events, local products, and bounties turn tsuchinoko into a collective pursuit.
claims.statement_id: Acara pencarian, produk daerah, dan hadiah membuat tsuchinoko menjadi sasaran pencarian bersama.
claims.quote: Elements like the venue, the search, treasure hunting, rallies, local products, and bounties turn the yokai into an object to be jointly sought

claims.statement: Possible tsuchinoko bones were found in Yoshii in 2000.
claims.statement_id: Pada tahun 2000 kerangka yang diduga tsuchinoko ditemukan di Yoshii.
claims.quote: The bones were found in May 2000, in the small town of Yoshii in Okayama Prefecture.

claims.statement: A biologist identified the bones as a malformed grass snake.
claims.statement_id: Ahli biologi menyatakan kerangka itu berasal dari ular rumput yang cacat.
claims.quote: a professor of biology declared that the remains were not those of a tsuchinoko but rather of a malformed grass snake.

claims.statement: A news account describes tsuchinoko as a fat snake not conclusively confirmed as real.
claims.statement_id: Media menggambarkan tsuchinoko sebagai ular gemuk yang keberadaannya belum dapat dipastikan.
claims.quote: the tsuchinoko, a creature resembling a fat snake that has never been conclusively confirmed as real

description.en: Tugarin (Russian: Тугарин) is a mythical creature in Russian byliny and fairy tales, which personifies evil and cruelty and appears in a dragon-like form. Tugarin is depicted as a giant and an opponent of Alyosha Popovich.

claims.statement: Tugarin is a mythical creature of Russian byliny and fairy tales personifying evil and cruelty, dragon-like in form, depicted as a giant and opponent of Alyosha Popovich.
claims.statement_id: Tugarin (Тугарин) adalah makhluk mitis dalam bylina dan dongeng Rusia yang mempersonifikasikan kejahatan dan kekejaman, berwujud mirip naga, digambarkan sebagai raksasa dan lawan Alyosha Popovich.
claims.quote: is a mythical creature in Russian byliny and fairy tales, which personifies evil and cruelty and appears in a dragon-like form. Tugarin is depicted as a giant and an opponent of Alyosha Popovich.

claims.statement: Tugarin has many names in Russian byliny and tales, such as Zmey Tugarin, Zmey Tugaretin and Zmeishche Tugarishche.
claims.statement_id: Tugarin punya banyak nama dalam bylina dan dongeng Rusia, seperti Zmey Tugarin, Zmey Tugaretin, dan Zmeishche Tugarishche.
claims.quote: Tugarin has many different names in Russian byliny and fairy tales, such as Zmey Tugarin, Zmey Tugaretin, Zmeishche Tugarishche, and others.

claims.statement: Though called a dragon, Tugarin largely keeps a human form and rides a horse; he seems winged and soars during the duel with Alyosha; some versions call the wings a paper contraption on his horse.
claims.statement_id: Walau disebut naga, Tugarin sebagian besar berwujud manusia dan menunggang kuda; ia tampak bersayap dan terbang saat duel dengan Alyosha; beberapa versi menyebut sayap itu alat dari kertas yang dipasang pada kudanya.
claims.quote: Tugarin, although spoken of as a dragon, largely retains an "anthropomorphic" form, and is seen riding a horse. It appears he has wings with which to fly, and he soars to the air during the duel with Alyosha.

claims.statement: Tugarin was a great glutton: he could stuff a whole wheel of bread in each cheek, then put a whole swan on his tongue and swallow it.
claims.statement_id: Tugarin sangat rakus: ia dapat menjejalkan satu roti bundar utuh di tiap pipi, lalu meletakkan seekor angsa utuh di lidahnya dan menelannya.
claims.quote: Tugarin was a great glutton, which is somewhat of a dragon-like trait. He could stuff a whole wheel of bread in each cheek, then deposit a whole swan on his tongue and swallow it.

claims.statement: Some commentators suggest Tugarin represents fire, since in some versions his torso is covered with fiery snakes used as weapons and he tries to strangle Alyosha with smoke.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian pengulas berpendapat Tugarin melambangkan unsur api, karena dalam beberapa versi tubuhnya diselimuti ular berapi yang dipakai sebagai senjata dan ia mencoba mencekik Alyosha dengan asap.
claims.quote: It has been suggested by some commentators that Tugarin represents the element of fire, since in some versions of "Alyosha Popovich", Tugarin's torso is covered with fiery snakes which he uses as a weapon, attempts to strangle Alyosha with smoke

claims.statement: Tugarin (also Zmey Tugarin, Tugarin Zmeyevich and others) is an evil bogatyr of Russian byliny and tales, opponent of the Russian bogatyrs Dobrynya Nikitich and Alyosha Popovich.
claims.statement_id: Tugarin (juga Zmey Tugarin, Tugarin Zmeyevich, dan lain-lain) adalah bogatyr jahat dalam bylina dan dongeng Rusia, lawan para bogatyr Rusia Dobrynya Nikitich dan Alyosha Popovich.
claims.quote: (также Змей Тугарин, Тугарин Змей, Змей Тугаретин, Тугарин Змеевич, Змеище Тугарище) — злой богатырь в русских былинах и сказках, противник русских богатырей Добрыни Никитича и Алёши Поповича.

claims.statement: The name Tugarin as a corruption of Tugar-Khan (Tugor-Khan of the Turkic Polovtsians) has been contested by an etymology from the root tug, "grief".
claims.statement_id: Nama Tugarin sebagai rusakan dari Tugar-Khan (Tugor-Khan dari bangsa Turkik Polovtsia) dibantah oleh etimologi dari akar kata tug, "duka".
claims.quote: The name Tugarin as a corruption of Tugar-Khan (Tugor-Khan ... of the Turkic Polovets), has been contested by an etymology from the root tug "grief".

claims.statement: Tugarin was linked with the historical Polovtsian khan Tugorkan.
claims.statement_id: Tugarin dikaitkan dengan khan Polovtsia historis Tugorkan.
claims.quote: Тугарина связывали с историческим половецким ханом Тугорканом.

claims.statement: A. K. Tolstoy's poem "Змей Тугарин" (Zmey Tugarin), 1867.
claims.statement_id: Puisi A. K. Tolstoy "Змей Тугарин" (Zmey Tugarin) tahun 1867.
claims.quote: Стихотворение А. К. Толстого «Змей Тугарин» (1867)

description.en: Türst (German: [tʏʁst]) is a legendary folkloric figure from the agricultural communities of Lucerne, dating to the pre-Christian era. He is described as a "dreadful huntsman", of whom people should be wary in stormy weather. Türst blows his hunting horn through villages in the tempestuous months preceding Epiphany, accompanied by a baying pack of three-legged hunting dogs. Specific beliefs about him vary from region to region.

claims.statement: Türst is a folk figure of Lucerne's farming communities dating to pre-Christian times, a 'dreadful huntsman' to beware of in stormy weather, who blows his horn through villages in the stormy months before Epiphany with a pack of three-legged hounds.
claims.statement_id: Türst adalah tokoh cerita rakyat dari komunitas petani Luzern yang berasal dari masa pra-Kristen, digambarkan sebagai "pemburu mengerikan" yang harus diwaspadai saat cuaca berbadai; ia meniup terompet berburu menembus desa-desa pada bulan-bulan berbadai menjelang Epifani bersama kawanan anjing berkaki tiga.
claims.quote: is a legendary folkloric figure from the agricultural communities of Lucerne, dating to the pre-Christian era. He is described as a "dreadful huntsman", of whom people should be wary in stormy weather. Türst blows his hunting horn through villages in the tempestuous months preceding Epiphany, accompanied by a baying pack of three-legged hunting dogs.

claims.statement: Türst's hallmark is his threat 'drü Schritt rechts, gang uswägs' ('step right; get out of my way'): a careless walker who fails to move aside in time is turned into a member of his dog pack.
claims.statement_id: Ciri khas Türst adalah ancaman "drü Schritt rechts, gang uswägs" ("ke kanan, minggir"): pejalan lalai yang tak menyingkir tepat waktu diubah menjadi anggota kawanan anjingnya.
claims.quote: Türst's distinguishing features are his threat "drü Schritt rechts, gang uswägs", or, roughly, "step right; get out of my way" in which the careless pedestrian is turned into a member of the dog-pack if he should fail to get out of Türst's way in time.

claims.statement: In Horw, Türst is followed by small hounds led by a one-eyed hound, his wife Sträggele, a hideous witch, and the Pfaffenkellnerin, the glowing-eyed ghost of a dead parson's mistress.
claims.statement_id: Di Horw, Türst diiringi anjing-anjing kecil yang dipimpin anjing bermata satu, istrinya Sträggele si penyihir buruk rupa, dan Pfaffenkellnerin, hantu kekasih seorang pastor yang bermata menyala.
claims.quote: In Horw, Türst is accompanied by small hounds, a leading hound with only one eye, Türst's wife, Sträggele, a hideous witch, and the Pfaffenkellnerin, the ghost of a deceased parson's mistress with glowing eyes.

claims.statement: In Rickenbach he appears in green hunting dress with a half-dog, half-pig pack; in Wolhusen people raised crosses against him, and a fallen cross brought farmers bad luck until set upright; the people of Pilatus call him a ghost and a 'dreadful huntsman'.
claims.statement_id: Di Rickenbach ia tampil berpakaian berburu hijau dengan kawanan setengah anjing setengah babi; di Wolhusen warga mendirikan salib untuk menghindarinya, dan bila salib roboh petani akan sial sampai salib ditegakkan; warga Pilatus menyebutnya hantu dan "pemburu mengerikan".
claims.quote: He appears in a green hunting costume in Rickenbach, accompanied by a pack of animals which are half dog and half pig. In Wolhusen, to avoid Türst, the citizens erected crosses. If a cross were to fall, the farmers would have bad luck until the cross stood straight again. The local people of Pilatus say that Türst is a ghost and a "dreadful huntsman"

claims.statement: Türst (also called Dürst) is a legendary figure from the Lucerne hinterland dating from heathen times, called the 'hellish huntsman'.
claims.statement_id: Türst (juga disebut Dürst) adalah tokoh legenda dari pedalaman Luzern yang berasal dari masa kafir dan disebut "pemburu neraka".
claims.quote: Der Türst (auch Dürst genannt) ist eine Sagenfigur aus dem Luzerner Hinterland, die noch aus heidnischen Zeiten stammt. Er wird als „höllischer Jäger“ bezeichnet

claims.statement: Barn doors should be left open at this time so Türst can hunt through unhindered; his wife Sträggele appears in some legends, and others say he terrifies dairy cows until they sicken and stop giving milk.
claims.statement_id: Konon pintu lumbung harus dibiarkan terbuka pada masa itu agar Türst dapat berburu menembus lumbung tanpa halangan; istrinya Sträggele muncul dalam sebagian legenda, dan legenda lain menyebut ia menakuti sapi perah hingga sakit dan berhenti menghasilkan susu.
claims.quote: It is also said that barn doors should stay open at this time, enabling Türst to hunt through the barn unhindered. Sträggele, his wife, appears in some Türst legends. Other legends say that Türst terrifies dairy cows, causing them to sicken and cease their milk production.

description.en: Two-Toed Tom is a legendary cryptid in the Southern United States who terrorized swamp residents in Florida and Alabama. The name originates from the legendary alligator having lost all but two toes on one or more feet to a steel trap.

claims.statement: Two-Toed Tom is a legendary cryptid of the Southern United States that terrorized swamp residents in Florida and Alabama.
claims.statement_id: Two-Toed Tom adalah kriptid legendaris di Amerika Serikat bagian selatan yang meneror penghuni rawa di Florida dan Alabama.
claims.quote: Two-Toed Tom is a legendary cryptid in the Southern United States who terrorized swamp residents in Florida and Alabama.

claims.statement: The name comes from the legendary alligator losing all but two toes on one or more feet to a steel trap.
claims.statement_id: Namanya berasal dari buaya aligator legendaris yang kehilangan jari-jarinya kecuali dua pada satu kaki atau lebih akibat perangkap baja.
claims.quote: The name originates from the legendary alligator having lost all but two toes on one or more feet to a steel trap.

claims.statement: One of the earliest written accounts is in Carl Carmer's 1934 book Stars Fell on Alabama.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu catatan tertulis tertuanya ada dalam buku Stars Fell on Alabama (1934) karya Carl Carmer.
claims.quote: One of the earliest written accounts can be traced to the 1934 book Stars Fell on Alabama, by Carl Carmer.

description.id: Udug (Sumeria: 𒌜), yang kelak dikenal dalam Akkadia sebagai utukku, adalah golongan iblis yang ambigu dari mitologi Mesopotamia kuno yang ditemukan dalam literatur Sumeria, Akad, Asyur, dan Babilonia. Mereka lahir di dunia bawah (Kur), sebagai makhluk yang berbeda dari dingir (Anu-nna-Ki dan Igigi), dan pada umumnya bersifat jahat, meskipun salah satu anggota iblis tersebut (Pazuzu) bersedia berselisih baik dengan sesama iblis maupun dengan para dewa, walau ia tetap digambarkan sebagai entitas yang memusuhi manusia. Istilah ini secara umum bermakna ganda dan kadang-kadang digunakan untuk merujuk pada iblis secara keseluruhan alih-alih jenis iblis tertentu. Belum ada representasi visual dari udug yang berhasil diidentifikasi, namun berbagai deskripsinya mengaitkan udug dengan ciri-ciri yang sering kali diberikan kepada iblis Mesopotamia kuno lainnya: bayangan gelap, ketiadaan cahaya di sekitarnya, racun, dan suara yang memekakkan telinga. Teks-teks Mesopotamia kuno yang masih bertahan yang memberikan instruksi untuk mengusir udug jahat dikenal sebagai teks-teks Udug Hul. Teks-teks ini menekankan peran udug jahat dalam menyebabkan penyakit dan peran pengusir setan dalam menyembuhkan penyakit tersebut.
description.en: The udug (Sumerian: 𒌜), later known in Akkadian as the utukku, were an ambiguous class of demons from ancient Mesopotamian mythology found in the literature of Sumer, Akkad, Assyria and Babylonia. They were born in the underworld (Kur), as a beings different from the dingir (Anu-nna-Ki and Igigi), and they were generally malicious, even if a member of demons (Pazuzu) was willing to clash both with other demons and with the gods, even if he is described as a presence hostile to humans. The word is generally ambiguous and is sometimes used to refer to demons as a whole rather than a specific kind of demon. No visual representations of the udug have yet been identified, but descriptions of it ascribe to it features often given to other ancient Mesopotamian demons: a dark shadow, absence of light surrounding it, poison, and a deafening voice. The surviving ancient Mesopotamian texts giving instructions for exorcizing the evil udug are known as the Udug Hul texts. These texts emphasize the evil udug's role in causing disease and the exorcist's role in curing the disease.
